```
enum ThumbnailTemplateSlotPolicy: String, Codable, Equatable, CaseIterable {
    case replaceFromProject  // pull the live project's asset / headline in
    case placeholder         // intentionally empty; creator fills it after applying
    case retained            // ship the template's own bytes/text (brand logo, channel name)
}
struct ThumbnailTemplateSlots: Codable, Equatable {
    static let currentVersion = 1
    var version: Int
    var backgroundImage: ThumbnailTemplateSlotPolicy   // -> ThumbnailDocument.imageData
    var profileImage:   ThumbnailTemplateSlotPolicy    // -> ThumbnailDocumentProfile.imageData
    var title:          ThumbnailTemplateSlotPolicy    // -> ThumbnailDocumentText.value
    var retainedLayerIDs: Set<String>     // template-local ids whose media SHIPS with the template
    var placeholderLayerIDs: Set<String>  // template-local image layers that arrive empty
    static var builtInDefaults  // background .replaceFromProject, profile .replaceFromProject, title .retained, empty sets
    static var personalDefaults // background .replaceFromProject, profile .replaceFromProject, title .placeholder
    init(from:)  // EVERY field decodeIfPresent, falling back to builtInDefaults
}
```
Invariant: the two id sets are disjoint. A content layer in neither set is a pure-style layer (shape/text) that ships verbatim because it carries no media.

NEW `ThumbnailMaker/Models/PersonalTemplateLibrary.swift` — pure value type, zero file IO, fully unit-testable:
```
struct PersonalTemplateLibrary: Codable, Equatable {
    static let currentVersion = 1
    static let maximumActiveTemplates = 60
    static let trashRetention: TimeInterval = 30*24*3600
    var version: Int; var templates: [ThumbnailTemplate]; var updatedAt: Date
    var active: [ThumbnailTemplate]   // deletedAt == nil; favourites first, then updatedAt desc, then name
    var trashed: [ThumbnailTemplate]
    func active(in: ThumbnailTemplateCategory) -> [ThumbnailTemplate]
    func template(id: String) -> ThumbnailTemplate?
    enum LibraryError: LocalizedError, Equatable {
        case libraryFull(limit: Int), notFound(String), builtInNotEditable(String), payloadTooLarge(bytes: Int, limit: Int)
    }
    @discardableResult mutating func insert(_:) throws -> ThumbnailTemplate  // rejects origin == .builtIn, enforces cap, uniquifies name
    mutating func update(id:mutate:) throws          // bumps template.updatedAt + library.updatedAt
    mutating func rename(id:to:) throws
    mutating func setFavorite(_:id:) throws
    mutating func setCategory(_:id:) throws
    @discardableResult mutating func duplicate(id:newID:now:) throws -> ThumbnailTemplate
    mutating func softDelete(id:now:) throws         // sets deletedAt, KEEPS the payload
    mutating func restore(id:) throws                // clears deletedAt, re-checks cap + name uniqueness
    mutating func purge(id:) throws                  // hard delete, only legal on a trashed item
    @discardableResult mutating func purgeExpired(now:) -> [String]
}
```
Name collisions are resolved by suffixing " 2", " 3", … (case/diacritic-insensitive compare) — never an error. Errors are reserved for the cap, not-found, built-in edits and the payload cap. `duplicate` produces a new id, `"<Name> Copy"`, `sourceTemplateID = source.id`, `isFavorite = false`.

`capture` (this is where "unrelated media is not copied into new projects" is enforced):
- rewrite every content-layer id to deterministic `tpl-0, tpl-1, …` in z order, so a template never carries the source project's UUIDs and re-capturing the same design yields byte-identical output.
- drop `document.imageData` unless `backgroundPolicy == .retained`; same for `profile.imageData` / `profilePolicy`.
- image content layers NOT in `retainedLayerIDs`: keep geometry/z/name, replace `imageData` with `Data()`, add the id to `placeholderLayerIDs`. (`ThumbnailImageLayerContent.imageData` is non-optional `Data` — `ThumbnailDocument.swift:324` — so empty `Data()` is the sentinel; `UIImage(data:)` returns nil, which the render path must tolerate. See risks.)
- clear `document.text.value` unless `titlePolicy == .retained`.
- `document.updatedAt = Date(timeIntervalSince1970: 0)` for stable equality; `document.macro.isEnabled = false` (batch numbering is project state, not layout).

`instantiate(over:mode:)`:
- `.styleOnly` — start from `existingDocument`; adopt ONLY `canvas.backgroundColor`, `text.color/size/selectedFontRawValue/transform/alignments`, and `export`. Layer set, images and headline untouched. No fresh ids needed. This is the explicit "apply a style" half of the brief.
- `.composition` — start from a copy of `template.document`, run `withFreshContentLayerIDs(idProvider)`, then resolve slots:
  - background: `.replaceFromProject` → `existingDocument.imageData`; `.retained` → template bytes; `.placeholder` → nil, and emit `.missingBackgroundImage` when the project had none either.
  - profile: same shape. When the template has no profile block but the policy is `.replaceFromProject` and the project HAS a profile image, splice the project's `profile` and append `defaultProfileLayer` — reproducing today's behaviour at `ThumbnailTemplate.swift:78-90`.
  - title: `.replaceFromProject` → `existingDocument.text.value`, falling back to the template's sample when the project title is empty; `.retained`/`.placeholder` → the template's own value.
  - layers in `placeholderLayerIDs` keep `Data()` and emit `.missingLayerImage(layerName:)`.
  - CRUCIALLY `.composition` does NOT copy the current project's content layers across — that is the behavioural difference from `makeDocument(preservingImagesFrom:)` and the reason a personal template applies cleanly: retained assets come from the template, replaceable ones from the named slots, and nothing else leaks.
  - finish with `layers.reconciledForCurrentOverlays(hasText:hasProfile:)`, set `updatedAt`.
- `makeDocument()` and `makeDocument(preservingImagesFrom:)` are left BYTE-IDENTICAL so built-ins, suggestions, ideas and all 8 existing template tests keep passing untouched.

risks:
1. PLACEHOLDER SENTINEL — `ThumbnailImageLayerContent.imageData` is non-optional `Data` (ThumbnailDocument.swift:324), so a placeholder image layer must carry `Data()`. Before shipping, the implementer MUST read `ThumbnailMaker/Views/Components/PreviewComponentView.swift` and the export path in `ThumbnailExporter.render` and confirm a layer whose `UIImage(data:)` is nil renders as nothing rather than crashing or force-unwrapping. Fallback if it does not: omit placeholder layers from `document.layers` at capture time and store their geometry inside `ThumbnailTemplateSlots` instead, re-materialising them when the creator supplies an image. Decide this BEFORE writing `capture`.

2. STORAGE SIZE — retained brand assets make template JSON large; 60 templates each holding a logo could reach tens of MB in Application Support. Mitigated by the 2 MB per-template / 25 MB per-library caps checked before any write, plus the existing atomic-write discipline so a rejected save never truncates the good file. Base64-in-JSON also inflates by ~33%; the caps are on encoded size, not raw bytes.

3. `ThumbnailTemplate.currentVersion` BUMP interacts with the pre-existing `version = max(decodedVersion, Self.currentVersion)` line (ThumbnailTemplate.swift:51) which silently upgrades every decoded version. Harmless for this feature, but do NOT "fix" it here — `thumbnailTemplateRoundTripsThroughCodable` (ThumbnailMakerTests.swift:257) asserts on exactly that behaviour.

4. IDEA-DERIVED TEMPLATES — `LocalThumbnailIdeaProvider.makeIdea` (ThumbnailIdea.swift:~145-168) mutates `template.id`/`name`/`document` on a BUILT-IN copy, so derived idea templates inherit `origin: .builtIn`. They must never reach `library.insert`; the `.builtInNotEditable` guard is the backstop, but the view layer should not offer "Save" on an idea card either.

5. SUGGESTION LOOKUPS still search only `ThumbnailTemplate.builtIns` (SimpleMakerViewModel.swift:739,805; PremiumMakerViewModel.swift:586,652). Personal templates will NOT appear in suggestions or title ideas. That is deliberate and out of scope; do not widen those lookups in this feature — it would pull the suggestion-provider files into the edit surface and risk `isActionableSuggestion` churn.

6. DO NOT TOUCH `ThumbnailDocumentLayer.reconciled` (ThumbnailDocument.swift:~600-640). Singleton ids `background`/`profile`/`text` are structural and must stay fixed; "fresh layer IDs" applies to CONTENT layers only. Rewriting a singleton id would make `reconciled` drop the layer and silently lose the text or profile overlay.

7. CONTENTION — `SimpleMakerViewModel.swift`, `PremiumMakerViewModel.swift`, `SimpleMakerView.swift`, `PremiumMakerView.swift` and `TemplateGalleryView.swift` are the busiest files in this repo and are already dirty in the working tree (git status shows M on all four view files). Slice B must be scheduled on a single implementer, after Slice A, and must preserve every unrelated uncommitted change. Slice A's one-file edit (`ThumbnailTemplate.swift`, currently clean) can run fully in parallel with other features.

8. UI-TEST IDENTIFIERS — `templateCard-youtube-bold-launch` is asserted in three places (AppStoreScreenshotTests.swift:39,42; ThumbnailMakerUITests.swift:1055) and feeds App Store screenshot capture via `scripts/capture-screenshots.sh`. Reordering gallery sections is safe; renaming or re-keying cards is not.

9. TRASH SEMANTICS — recoverable delete keeps the full payload for 30 days, so a creator who deletes 20 heavy templates still occupies their storage. `purgeExpired` runs on every `load()`, which is the only sweep; there is no background task. Acceptable, but the management UI should show trash size.

Codable back-compat: hand-written `init(from:)` using `decodeIfPresent` with defaults for EVERY field except `variants` (version -> currentVersion, projectName -> "thumbnail", activeSlot -> first present slot, preferredSlot -> nil, editorMode -> .simple), then `self = normalized()`. API (all mutating methods on the struct, pure, no I/O):
- `init(seedDocument:editorMode:projectName:now:)` — one variant in slot `.a`, name "Variant A", activeSlot `.a`, preferredSlot nil.
- `var activeDocument: ThumbnailDocument` (falls back to the lowest present slot if activeSlot went missing).
- `func document(for:) -> ThumbnailDocument?`, `func variant(for:) -> ThumbnailVariant?`, `func contains(_:) -> Bool`
- `var canAddVariant: Bool { variants.count < Self.maxVariantCount }`
- `var nextFreeSlot: ThumbnailVariantSlot?` — lowest unused slot.
- `mutating func duplicateVariant(from:now:) -> ThumbnailVariantSlot?` — deep-copies the source document (all value types, so a plain assignment IS the deep copy) into `nextFreeSlot`, name = destination slot's `defaultName`, sets it active, returns the new slot; nil when full. LAYER IDs ARE PRESERVED VERBATIM (documents are independent, so cross-variant ID reuse is harmless, and it keeps `selectedLayer` resolvable when the user switches variants).
- `mutating func removeVariant(_:) -> Bool` — refuses to remove the last remaining variant. Remaining slots are NOT re-lettered (a set may legitimately be {A, C}); re-lettering would silently rename a design the user already reasoned about and already exported. If the removed slot was active, activate the lowest remaining; if it was preferred, clear preferred.
- `mutating func setPreferred(_:)` / `mutating func clearPreferred()` — only accepts a slot that exists.
- `mutating func rename(slot:to:)` — trim; empty falls back to `slot.defaultName`; clamp to 40 chars.
- `mutating func updateDocument(_:for:now:)` — replaces that variant's document and bumps its `updatedAt` and the set's; no-op when byte-equal.
- `func normalized() -> Self` — dedupe slots (first wins), drop past `maxVariantCount`, sort by slot, guarantee >= 1 variant (seeds `.a` with a default document if empty), force `activeSlot` and `preferredSlot` to existing slots.

EXPLICIT ANTI-REQUIREMENT, enforced by review and by a test asserting no such symbols exist: nothing in this feature may compute, store, persist, or display a predicted or measured winner, a CTR, a score, or a ranking. `preferredSlot` is set ONLY by an explicit user gesture. === B. NEW SERVICES ===

B1. ThumbnailMaker/Services/ThumbnailVariantAssetLibrary.swift — REVERSIBLE RECIPE OVER IMMUTABLE ORIGINALS
Three full documents each holding 4K PNG payloads would triple the draft file. A/B/C almost always share the same background photo, so image bytes are stored ONCE, content-addressed, and each variant document references them.

```swift
struct ThumbnailVariantAssetRefs: Codable, Equatable {
    var backgroundImage: String?              // digest for document.imageData
    var profileImage: String?                 // digest for document.profile?.imageData
    var contentLayers: [String: String]       // layer.id -> digest, for .image layer content
}

enum ThumbnailVariantAssetLibrary {
    static func digest(_ data: Data) -> String                       // CryptoKit SHA256 hex (system framework)
    static func dehydrate(_ document: ThumbnailDocument,
                          into assets: inout [String: Data])
                          -> (document: ThumbnailDocument, refs: ThumbnailVariantAssetRefs)
    static func hydrate(_ document: ThumbnailDocument,
                        refs: ThumbnailVariantAssetRefs,
                        assets: [String: Data])
                        -> (document: ThumbnailDocument, missingDigests: Set<String>)
}
```
Dehydrate walks `imageData`, `profile?.imageData`, and every `.image` layer content; stores bytes in `assets` keyed by digest; sets `imageData`/`profile.imageData` to nil and `ThumbnailImageLayerContent.imageData` (non-optional, ThumbnailDocument.swift:327) to `Data()`. Hydrate reverses it. This is a pure recipe: the originals are never re-encoded, cropped, or degraded, so N save/load round trips are lossless — the same invariant ThumbnailImagePersistenceTests.swift already pins for single drafts.

Hydration NEVER throws on a missing digest. It returns the document with that payload absent plus `missingDigests`, so a partially corrupt file still opens (a layer with empty Data yields `UIImage(data:) == nil` and simply does not render; `reconciledForCurrentOverlays` keeps it because `content != nil`). "Old documents MUST still open" extends to "damaged variant files must still open".

(The existing encoder/decoder are `private extension`s in ThumbnailDraftStore.swift, so this file declares its own — no edit to that file.)

```swift

final class ThumbnailVariantStore {

    static func defaultFileURL(for kind: ThumbnailDraftStore.DraftKind) -> URL

    static func siblingURL(of draftURL: URL, kind: ThumbnailDraftStore.DraftKind) -> URL
        // draftURL.deletingLastPathComponent() + "{simple,premium}-maker-variants.json"
    func save(_ set: ThumbnailVariantSet) throws
    func load() throws -> ThumbnailVariantLoadResult?          // nil when the file is absent
```

```swift

    var version: Int
    var updatedAt: Date
    var editorMode: ThumbnailDocumentEditorMode
```

Error handling required here:
- Size guard: if the encoded payload exceeds 120 MB, throw `ThumbnailVariantStoreError.setTooLarge(byteCount:)` with a `LocalizedError` message naming the limit. The legacy single-draft save in the view model runs FIRST and independently, so the active design is never lost when the variant set is too big to persist.
- Redundant-write guard: cache the last written payload's digest and early-return when unchanged. The editor autosaves on a 0.6 s debounce (SimpleMakerViewModel.swift:600-611) and would otherwise re-serialize three documents on every keystroke pause.

HIGH VALUE, ZERO CONFLICT: the entire model/service layer (7 new source files + 4 new test files) modifies NO existing file. `ThumbnailDocument`, `ThumbnailDocumentHistory` and `ThumbnailDraftStore` are composed, never edited. Sections A and B of the plan can be scheduled against a completely empty lock set.

1. Draft-file size explosion. Three documents each carrying 4K PNG payloads (ThumbnailDocument.swift:1382-1401 deliberately stores PNG, not JPEG, to preserve cutout alpha) could triple the draft. Mitigated by content-addressed asset dedup in ThumbnailVariantAssetLibrary — A/B/C sharing a background store its bytes once — plus a 120 MB typed save error. Residual risk: three genuinely different 4K backgrounds still cost 3x, and PHPhotoLibrary/JSON round trips of that size on a low-memory device could be slow. Test 15 pins the dedup; the size guard bounds the worst case.

2. Autosave amplification. The 0.6 s debounce (SimpleMakerViewModel.swift:600-611) fires `saveDraftNow()` constantly; naively that now re-serializes and rewrites three documents per pause. Mitigated by the last-written-digest early return in ThumbnailVariantStore.save. If it were skipped, typing in the editor would become janky — this is the single most likely performance regression.

3. Breaking DraftSaveStateTests. The existing tests inject a `ThumbnailDraftStore` at a temp path and assert `.saved`/`.failed` transitions. If the variant store defaults to the real Application Support container instead of a sibling of `draftStore.fileURL`, those tests will write to the user's real container and the "save fails, last good draft survives" case (DraftSaveStateTests.swift:78) will stop failing as designed. The `siblingOf:` derivation in C1 is not optional.

4. Stale layer selection on switch. `selectedLayer` lives in the VIEW (`@State`, SimpleMakerView.swift:23), not the view model, and holds a layer ID that may not exist in the incoming variant. `normalizeSelectedLayer()` already exists at SimpleMakerView.swift:612 but must be called after every variant switch/duplicate/delete. Missing this yields an invisible selection and dead manipulation handles — an easy bug to ship.

5. Undo redirection subtlety. The computed-property trick in C2 relies on Swift's get-modify-set for mutating calls on settable computed properties. It is correct, but it means `history.record(...)` reads and writes a dictionary entry keyed by `variantSet.activeSlot`. If any code path mutates `activeSlot` BETWEEN the get and a later set (it does not today, but a future refactor could), an edit would land in the wrong slot's stack. Guard by making `selectVariant` the only writer of `activeSlot` in the view model and by tests 29-30.

6. Aspect-ratio mismatch across variants. Each variant owns its own `canvas.aspectRatioRawValue`, so "compare at identical sizes" is only honest if one ratio wins. Forcing the active variant's ratio letterboxes a 9:16 variant into a 16:9 pane. Reporting `mismatchedSlots` rather than silently distorting is the chosen tradeoff; a reviewer may prefer disallowing mixed ratios inside a set entirely — that would be a smaller model but loses a legitimate use case.

7. Spec-compliance risk on "preferred". It is easy for a later contributor to add a "which is winning?" affordance. The plan states the anti-requirement explicitly and test 22 asserts the export name contains none of winner/best/top/ctr/score, but only code review keeps a scoring UI out. The three-variant cap and the watch-time (not CTR) basis of YouTube Test & Compare mean the app must never imply it can predict or measure the outcome.

8. Slot letters are not re-lettered on delete, so a set can be {A, C}. This is deliberate (renaming C to B would change a filename the user may already have uploaded), but it will look like a bug to anyone who has not read the rationale. Document it in the type and in test 4.

9. Premium batch generation. `PremiumMakerViewModel.commitEditorStateNow` guards on `isBatchGenerating` (:457). The variant refresh line must sit inside that guard or a macro batch run will rewrite the variant set once per generated image.

10. Two mirrored view models. SimpleMakerViewModel and PremiumMakerViewModel are near-duplicates; the wiring must be applied twice and will drift if the two implementers diverge. Keeping all real logic in `ThumbnailVariantSet` / `ThumbnailVariantHistoryBook` (slice 1) holds each view-model diff to roughly 40 lines and makes the drift risk cosmetic.

11. New framework import: CryptoKit for SHA-256 digests. System framework, no dependency risk, currently unused in the project. If a reviewer objects, `[Data: String]` dedup works identically (Data is Hashable and `==` compares fully) at the cost of unstable ids across saves.

GOAL: one persisted, reversible framing recipe per image; one pure geometry function that preview, export, and the crop UI all call; originals never re-encoded.

=== 1. NEW MODEL: ThumbnailMaker/Models/ThumbnailImageFrameRecipe.swift ===

```swift
enum ThumbnailImageFitMode: String, Codable, CaseIterable, Equatable {
    case fit      // letterbox — today's behavior, the back-compat default
    case fill     // aspect-fill + crop to the frame (the market fix)
    case stretch  // explicit, opt-in distortion; never a default
}

struct ThumbnailImageFrameRecipe: Codable, Equatable {
    var fitRawValue: String        // ThumbnailImageFitMode
    var focusX: Double             // 0...1, normalized focal point in DISPLAY-oriented source space
    var focusY: Double             // 0...1
    var zoom: Double               // 1.0...8.0, multiplier over the fit/fill baseline scale
    var cropAspectRatio: Double?   // w/h of the visible window; nil = use the destination frame's aspect

    static let identity     = ThumbnailImageFrameRecipe(fit: .fit,  focusX: 0.5, focusY: 0.5, zoom: 1, cropAspectRatio: nil)
    static let fillCentered = ThumbnailImageFrameRecipe(fit: .fill, focusX: 0.5, focusY: 0.5, zoom: 1, cropAspectRatio: nil)

    var fit: ThumbnailImageFitMode { get { .init(rawValue: fitRawValue) ?? .fit } set { fitRawValue = newValue.rawValue } }
    var isIdentity: Bool
    static let zoomLimits: ClosedRange<Double> = 1.0...8.0
}
```
The memberwise-style `init` CLAMPS on construction: `focusX/Y` into `0...1`, `zoom` into `zoomLimits` (also rejecting NaN/infinite → falls back to the default), `cropAspectRatio` to `nil` when non-finite or `<= 0`. `init(from:)` routes through the same clamping so a hand-edited/corrupt JSON can never produce NaN geometry.

Pure recipe transforms (model layer, no SwiftUI — this is what makes "one completed gesture = one undo step" testable):
```swift
extension ThumbnailImageFrameRecipe {
    // Convert a completed pan (points, in frame space) + magnification into a new recipe.
    static func applying(panTranslation: CGSize, magnification: CGFloat,
                         to base: Self, sourceSize: CGSize, frameSize: CGSize) -> Self
    // Vision returns bottom-left-origin normalized rects; convert to focal+zoom+fill.
    static func framing(visionCropRect: CGRect, sourceSize: CGSize, frameSize: CGSize) -> Self
    // Frame aspect for a content layer whose box is derived from the image.
    func effectiveAspectRatio(sourceAspectRatio: CGFloat) -> CGFloat
}
```
`applying` converts the pan into a focal delta (`-translation / renderSize`), multiplies `zoom` by `magnification`, then re-clamps. `framing(visionCropRect:)` flips y (`1 - (origin.y + height)`), takes the crop centre as focal, and sets `zoom = min(1/cropW, 1/cropH)` clamped to `zoomLimits`, `fit = .fill` — so the face crop becomes fully reversible.

=== 2. NEW SERVICE: ThumbnailMaker/Models/ThumbnailImageGeometry.swift — THE one geometry function ===

```swift
enum ThumbnailImageGeometry {
    struct Solution: Equatable {
        var frameSize: CGSize    // clipping frame
        var renderSize: CGSize   // size handed to the resizable Image
        var offset: CGSize       // offset of the image inside the frame (points)
        var sourceRect: CGRect   // normalized rect of the source that ends up visible
    }
    static func solve(sourceSize: CGSize, frameSize: CGSize,
                      recipe: ThumbnailImageFrameRecipe) -> Solution
}
```
Algorithm (deterministic, no UIKit/SwiftUI types beyond CGGeometry):
1. Degenerate guard: any of `sourceSize.width/height`, `frameSize.width/height` is `<= 0`, NaN, or infinite → return `Solution(frameSize: frameSize, renderSize: frameSize, offset: .zero, sourceRect: CGRect(0,0,1,1))`. Never divides by zero.
2. `.stretch` → `renderSize = frameSize`, `offset = .zero`, `sourceRect = unit`. Focal/zoom are documented as ignored.
3. `baseScale = fit == .fill ? max(fw/sw, fh/sh) : min(fw/sw, fh/sh)`; `scale = baseScale * clampedZoom`; `renderSize = sourceSize * scale`.
4. Per axis: if `renderSize >= frameSize`, `offset = clamp(frameCenter - focus * renderSize, frameSize - renderSize ... 0)` — the clamp is what guarantees no transparent gutter is ever exposed in `.fill`, no matter the focal point. If `renderSize < frameSize` (fit, zoom 1), centre it: `offset = (frameSize - renderSize) / 2`.
5. `sourceRect = CGRect(x: max(0, -offset.x/renderSize.w), y: max(0, -offset.y/renderSize.h), width: min(1, fw/renderSize.w), height: min(1, fh/renderSize.h))`.

KEY INVARIANT (this is the testable statement of "preview and export share one geometry function"): `solve` is scale-invariant — `solve(src, frame: k*f, r).sourceRect == solve(src, frame: f, r).sourceRect` for all `k > 0`. Preview at ~350pt and export at 1920×1080 therefore frame identical pixels. Provable with zero view code.

plan:
## Container choice: a file package (directory bundle), not a zip

iOS Foundation ships no public zip writer/reader, so a `.zip` container would mean a third-party dependency or the awkward `NSFileCoordinator(.forUploading)` trick. Use an Apple **file package**: a directory with extension `.tmproj` whose UTType conforms to `com.apple.package`. Files.app shows it as one item, `FileDocument` handles it natively via `FileWrapper(directoryWithFileWrappers:)`, and assets stay real, inspectable files.

Layout:
```
MyProject.tmproj/
  manifest.json        (schema, identity, asset table, bindings, preview path)
  document.json        (exactly what JSONEncoder produces for ThumbnailDocument, minus pixel blobs)
  assets/<sha256>.png  (immutable original pixels, content-addressed, deduped)
  preview.png          (rendered flattened preview, informational only)
```

## The load-bearing decision: externalize blobs WITHOUT touching ThumbnailDocument.swift

`ThumbnailImageLayerContent.imageData` is a non-optional `Data` (`ThumbnailDocument.swift:327`) and the document's/profile's are `Data?`. Making them optional or adding `assetID` fields would mean editing `ThumbnailDocument.swift` — the single highest-contention model file (FEATURE-03 reversible framing, FEATURE-04 text styles, FEATURE-05 templates all want it).

Instead, keep the document type untouched and hold the blob→asset mapping **in the manifest**, keyed by an explicit slot enum:

```swift
enum ThumbnailProjectAssetSlot: Codable, Equatable, Hashable {
    case backgroundImage              // encodes as "background"
    case profileImage                 // encodes as "profile"
    case layerImage(layerID: String)  // encodes as "layer:<id>"
    // singleValueContainer <-> String; unknown prefixes decode as nil and are skipped
}
```

The writer copies the document, sets `document.imageData = nil`, `document.profile?.imageData = nil`, and each image layer's `content.imageData = Data()`, recording each stripped blob under its slot. The reader re-binds. Consequences:
- `document.json` is produced/consumed by `ThumbnailDocument`'s existing `Codable` conformance verbatim, so its whole migration ladder (`init(from:)` at `ThumbnailDocument.swift:184-206`, the `ThumbnailDocumentProfile` legacy-position path at `:278-322`, the `decodeIfPresent`-with-default style everywhere) keeps working unchanged.
- Any field FEATURE-03/04 adds to the document is carried through the package for free.
- Back-compat is trivially preserved because zero existing `Codable` types change. New optional-with-default fields live only in the brand-new manifest type.
- If a future feature adds a new image-bearing field, it adds one `case` to `ThumbnailProjectAssetSlot` — a change entirely inside the new files.

This is a reversible recipe over immutable originals: transforms/sizes/colors/z-order stay in `document.json`; the original pixels live once each in `assets/`, content-addressed by SHA-256 so a duplicated layer costs one copy.

### 4. `ThumbnailMaker/Services/ThumbnailProjectPackageWriter.swift`
```swift
struct ThumbnailProjectPackageWriter {
    static func makePackage(from document: ThumbnailDocument,
                            name: String,
                            projectID: String = UUID().uuidString,
                            createdAt: Date = Date(),
                            updatedAt: Date = Date(),
                            previewPNGData: Data? = nil,
                            generatorVersion: String? = ...) throws -> ThumbnailProjectPackage
    static func fileWrapper(for package: ThumbnailProjectPackage) throws -> FileWrapper
    static func write(_ package: ThumbnailProjectPackage, to url: URL) throws   // test/CLI seam
}
```
`makePackage` walks the three slot families in a single `extractAssets(from:)` helper, hashes each non-empty blob with `CryptoKit.SHA256`, dedupes on the hex digest, sniffs PNG/JPEG magic bytes to pick the extension + UTI (documents are PNG today per `ThumbnailDocument.encodedImageData(from:)` at `:1382-1400`, but handle JPEG since older drafts and `SimpleThumbnailDraft` at `ThumbnailDraftStore.swift:104-105` produced JPEG). It enforces the count/size ceilings at write time too, so the app can never emit a package it would then refuse to read.
`fileWrapper` builds `FileWrapper(directoryWithFileWrappers:)` with a nested `assets` directory wrapper; `write` calls `wrapper.write(to:options:[.atomic], originalContentsURL: nil)`.

### 5. `ThumbnailMaker/Services/ThumbnailProjectPackageReader.swift`
```swift
struct ThumbnailProjectPackageReader {
    static func readPackage(at url: URL) throws -> ThumbnailProjectPackage
    static func package(from wrapper: FileWrapper) throws -> ThumbnailProjectPackage
}
```
`readPackage(at:)` wraps the URL access in `url.startAccessingSecurityScopedResource()` / `defer { stopAccessing... }` (required for `fileImporter` results), builds `FileWrapper(url:options:[.immediate])`, delegates to `package(from:)`.

**Validation order — every check runs and throws before anything is handed back, so a failure cannot have mutated the open project:**
1. `wrapper.isDirectory` else `.notAPackage`.
2. `manifest.json` present (`.manifestMissing`), ≤ 1 MB (`.manifestTooLarge`), decodes (`.manifestUnreadable`).
3. `formatIdentifier == ThumbnailProjectPackageLayout.formatIdentifier` else `.unsupportedFormatIdentifier`.
4. **Future-version gate:** `minimumReaderVersion <= supportedSchemaVersion` else `.unsupportedFutureVersion(found: minimumReaderVersion, supported: 1)`. Also `schemaVersion >= 1` else `.unsupportedLegacyVersion`. This is a *read-only* rejection — the reader never writes, so the source file is untouched, satisfying "reject unsupported future versions without overwriting them". Writers of a future v2 that stays v1-readable set `minimumReaderVersion: 1` and v1 reads it, dropping unknown manifest keys.
5. `assets.count <= 64` else `.assetCountExceeded`.
6. **Path validation, per record.** Reject if `path` is empty, absolute (`hasPrefix("/")`), contains `..`, `\`, `:` or a null byte, splits into anything other than exactly `["assets", <file>]`, or `<file> != "\(id).\(ext)"`. Then **look the file up inside the `assets` sub-wrapper by its last path component only** — never by constructing a `URL` from the manifest string. This is what makes path traversal impossible and what makes "never depends on the source device path" literally true. Failures → `.assetPathRejected`.
7. Every referenced asset file exists → else `.assetMissing(id:)`.
8. `record.byteCount == data.count` else `.assetSizeMismatch`; `data.count <= 32 MB` else `.assetTooLarge`.
9. Sum of all asset bytes + document + preview ≤ 192 MB else `.packageTooLarge`.
10. `SHA256.hash(data:)` hex == `record.sha256` (and == `record.id`) else `.assetChecksumMismatch`.
11. `UIImage(data:) != nil` for each asset else `.assetUndecodable`.
12. `document.json` present/≤8 MB/decodes as `ThumbnailDocument` else `.documentMissing` / `.documentTooLarge` / `.documentUnreadable`.
13. Every binding's `assetID` is in the asset table, and every binding slot that names a layer refers to a layer id actually present in the decoded document → else `.bindingUnresolved(slot:)`. Assets present but unbound are tolerated (dropped) and do not fail.
14. `preview.png`, if declared, must be ≤ 8 MB and decode; a bad preview is **non-fatal** — it is dropped, since it carries no editable state.

### 6. `ThumbnailMaker/Services/ThumbnailProjectImporter.swift`
```swift
struct ThumbnailProjectImportResult: Equatable {
    var document: ThumbnailDocument          // assets re-bound, IDs fresh
    var manifest: ThumbnailProjectPackageManifest
    var projectID: String
    var name: String
    var layerIDMap: [String: String]
    var didRenameForCollision: Bool
    var isCrossEditorImport: Bool
}

struct ThumbnailProjectImporter {
    static func importedCopy(of package: ThumbnailProjectPackage,
                             into editorMode: ThumbnailDocumentEditorMode,
                             existingProjectIDs: Set<String> = [],
                             existingNames: [String] = [],
                             now: Date = Date(),
                             idFactory: () -> String = { UUID().uuidString }) throws -> ThumbnailProjectImportResult
    static func uniqueName(_ candidate: String, among existing: [String]) -> String
}
```
Behaviour:
- **Re-bind assets.** Put bytes back into `document.imageData`, `document.profile?.imageData`, and each image layer's `content.imageData`. A binding that cannot be resolved throws (already validated) — never a silently blank layer.
- **Always a new copy.** `projectID = idFactory()` unconditionally; `existingProjectIDs` is only used to assert the minted id is unused (retry loop, bounded), so import can never collide with or overwrite an existing project even once FEATURE-01 lands.
- **Fresh layer identities.** Every layer whose id is not `ThumbnailDocumentLayer.backgroundID` / `.profileID` / `.textID` (`ThumbnailDocument.swift:457-459`) gets a new id from `idFactory()`, recorded in `layerIDMap` and applied consistently (also to bindings before re-binding). The three singleton ids are deliberately preserved because `ThumbnailDocumentLayer.reconciled(_:hasText:hasProfile:)` (`:611-659`) keys on them.
- **Name collisions** → `uniqueName` appends " 2", " 3", … ; `didRenameForCollision` reports it. Empty/whitespace-only name falls back to "Imported Project".
- **Normalize and heal.** `document.updatedAt = now`; layers passed through `reconciledForCurrentOverlays(hasText:hasProfile:)` (`:662-664`) so a hand-edited package cannot yield duplicate singletons, orphan records, or content-less content layers; layers re-sorted by `zIndex`; content-layer `zIndex` re-based from `contentLayerZIndexStart` preserving relative order.
- **Cross-editor import.** If `manifest.editorModeRawValue != editorMode.rawValue`, set `isCrossEditorImport = true`. Importing a premium package into Simple drops profile + macro state (`makeSimpleConfiguration()` ignores both, `ThumbnailDocument.swift:1326-1330`); the view model surfaces a notice rather than blocking. `document.editorMode` is rewritten to the destination editor.
- `existingProjectIDs`/`existingNames` default to empty so today's callers pass nothing; they are the seam FEATURE-01's library fills in.

## Migration & back-compat

- Zero changes to any existing `Codable` type, so every stored draft keeps decoding through the unchanged `ThumbnailDraftStore.loadDocument()` path (`:206-223`) including its `SimpleThumbnailDraft` legacy fallback.
- Package schema starts at 1. Every manifest field except `formatIdentifier`/`schemaVersion`/`minimumReaderVersion` is `decodeIfPresent`-with-default, so a v2 writer that only *adds* fields produces packages a v1 reader still opens.
- Forward rejection is explicit and non-destructive (`minimumReaderVersion` gate, reader never writes).
- The embedded `document.json` still carries `ThumbnailDocument.version`, so once inside the app it rides the document's own existing migration.

2. **Platform/type slice.** New file 7 + `Info.plist`. Trivial, no Swift file shared with slice 1 or 3.
3. **UI slice.** The two view models + the two views. Depends on slice 1's API surface existing but touches none of its files.

risks:
**A model/service-only slice is not just viable, it is most of the feature.** New files 1-6 (`ThumbnailProjectPackage`, `ThumbnailProjectPackageError`, `UTType+ThumbnailProject`, the writer, the reader, the importer) plus all three test files land with **zero edits to any SwiftUI view and zero edits to either view model**. The whole round trip — build a package from a `ThumbnailDocument`, write it to a temp directory, read it back with a fresh `FileManager`, validate it, import it as an editable copy with new IDs — is exercisable head-to-toe from swift-testing without a view in sight. Every acceptance criterion except the literal Files.app picker chrome is covered by that slice. Schedule it first and alone; the view/view-model slice can follow behind it without ever touching one of its files.

**Risks and mitigations**

1. *Slot enumeration drift (the main structural risk).* Because blobs are externalized by an explicit `ThumbnailProjectAssetSlot` enum rather than by changing `ThumbnailDocument`, a future feature that adds a new image-bearing field (FEATURE-03's reversible framing is the likely one — it may add an "original asset" reference to image layers) would have its pixels silently left inline in `document.json` rather than externalized. Mitigation: add a test that asserts `document.json` stays under a small byte ceiling for a fixture with megabyte images — it fails loudly the moment a new blob field appears. Also leave a comment on the enum naming the invariant.

2. *File-contention with FEATURE-03/04/05.* All three want `ThumbnailMaker/Models/ThumbnailDocument.swift`. This design deliberately does **not** touch it. It also does not touch `ThumbnailDraftStore.swift`, `ThumbnailDocumentHistory.swift`, `ThumbnailExporter.swift`, `ThumbnailFileDocument.swift`, or `project.pbxproj`. The only genuinely contended files are the two views and the two view models, all in the UI slice.

3. *FEATURE-01 is a declared dependency and does not exist.* Import therefore targets "the currently open editor" rather than a project library. `projectName` is a plain `@Published var` on the view model, not a persisted library entity — it will not survive relaunch until FEATURE-01 lands. `importedCopy(of:into:existingProjectIDs:existingNames:)` already takes the library's inputs as defaulted parameters, so FEATURE-01 plugs in without changing the signature. Flag this to the parent: if FEATURE-01 lands in the same milestone, the two implementers must agree on who owns `projectName`.

4. *Cross-editor import is lossy.* A premium package imported into Simple Maker drops the circular profile and macro/batch settings, because `makeSimpleConfiguration()` (`ThumbnailDocument.swift:1326-1330`) ignores both. The design surfaces a notice and proceeds rather than blocking or auto-switching tabs — auto-switching would require editing `ContentView.swift` and plumbing a cross-tab channel, widening the edit surface for little gain. If the reviewer wants the import to land in the matching editor, that is a follow-up that adds `ContentView.swift` to the list.

5. *`.fileExporter` and file packages.* `FileDocument.fileWrapper(configuration:)` returning a directory wrapper works, but Files.app only renders it as a single item if the exported UTType conforms to `com.apple.package` **and** `LSTypeIsPackage` is set. If the `Info.plist` declaration is wrong the export silently appears as a browsable folder — cosmetically wrong, functionally still importable. This is the one part unit tests cannot catch; it must be checked by hand on device.

6. *Security-scoped URLs.* `fileImporter` hands back URLs that require `startAccessingSecurityScopedResource()`. Forgetting the paired `stopAccessingSecurityScopedResource()` leaks a sandbox extension. The reader owns both sides in a `defer`; do not let the view model open the URL itself.

7. *Memory on large packages.* The reader materializes every asset in memory before validating (needed for checksums). With the 192 MB total ceiling that is a real spike on older devices. The ceilings are deliberately conservative; if it proves a problem, stream the SHA-256 with `FileHandle` chunks rather than raising the limit.

8. *`ThumbnailDocument.version` clamping.* `init(from:)` does `version = max(decodedVersion, Self.currentVersion)` (`ThumbnailDocument.swift:206`), so a package containing a document at a *future* document version decodes without complaint and is then re-saved having dropped unknown fields. The package-level `minimumReaderVersion` gate is what actually blocks this, since the writer records `documentVersion` in the manifest — so the reader should **also** reject `manifest.documentVersion > ThumbnailDocument.currentVersion` as `.unsupportedFutureVersion`. Do not "fix" the clamp in `ThumbnailDocument.swift`; that file is off-limits for this feature and changing it would break draft loading for anyone mid-migration.

9. *Preview generation on the main actor.* `ThumbnailExporter.render(content:options:)` is `@MainActor` and uses `ImageRenderer`. Generating the package preview at export time adds a main-thread hitch. Keep the preview small (640×360) and treat failure as non-fatal — the preview carries no editable state.

10. *Test flakiness from shared temp state.* Every disk test must use a unique `UUID()` subdirectory with a `defer` cleanup, as the existing persistence tests do. Tests that assert "the on-disk file is unchanged after a failed read" must compare bytes, not modification dates.

```swift
enum ThumbnailTextAlignment: String, Codable, CaseIterable, Equatable { case leading, center, trailing }

struct ThumbnailTextStyle: Codable, Equatable {
    // Outline (fractions of FONT SIZE)
    var outlineWidth: Double            // 0...0.25, 0 == none
    var outlineColor: ThumbnailDocumentColor
    // Shadow (fractions of FONT SIZE; alpha lives in the colour)
    var isShadowEnabled: Bool
    var shadowRadius: Double            // 0...0.5
    var shadowOffsetX: Double           // -0.5...0.5
    var shadowOffsetY: Double           // -0.5...0.5
    var shadowColor: ThumbnailDocumentColor
    // Background panel (fractions of FONT SIZE)
    var panelColor: ThumbnailDocumentColor?   // nil == no panel
    var panelCornerRadius: Double       // 0...2
    var horizontalPadding: Double       // 0...2
    var verticalPadding: Double         // 0...2
    // Spacing (fractions of FONT SIZE)
    var lineSpacing: Double             // -0.2...1.5
    var letterSpacing: Double           // -0.2...1.0  (applied via Text.tracking)
    // Layout
    var alignmentRawValue: String       // ThumbnailTextAlignment
    var maxWidthFraction: Double        // 0.2...1.0 — fraction of CANVAS WIDTH (the one deliberate exception to the font-size rule; it is a layout bound, not a type effect)
    var lineLimit: Int?                 // nil == unlimited, else 1...10
    var minimumScaleFactor: Double      // 0.2...1.0
    var presetID: String?               // provenance only, never affects rendering
}
```

UNIT RULE (write it as a doc comment): every metric except `maxWidthFraction` is a fraction of the resolved font size; `maxWidthFraction` is a fraction of canvas width. Because the font size is itself `canvasHeight * textSize`, every resolved point value scales linearly with the canvas — that IS the canvas/export parity guarantee, and it is exactly testable (see test plan).

RISKS:
1. Legacy exactness vs parity is a genuine tension, resolved deliberately. Today's shadow (`radius: 3, x: 1, y: 1`) is in absolute points, so it is ~5.5x relatively tighter in a 1280x720 export than in the ~350x197 editor preview. The design keeps that literal behaviour for `style == nil` (old documents open pixel-identical) and switches to scale-relative metrics the moment the user touches a control. Consequence: the FIRST style edit changes the small-preview shadow slightly (it shrinks to match the export). This must be stated in the PR description; it is a fix, but it is a visible change and a reviewer will notice it.
2. `PremiumMakerView.swift:1224-1240` builds `PremiumMakerConfigurationModel` memberwise. A defaulted `textStyle` still compiles there, so the compiler will NOT catch the omission — batch/macro exports would silently render unstyled. This is the single most likely lost-work bug in the whole feature.
3. The selection-chrome proxies (PreviewComponentView.swift:338-343, PremiumPreviewComponentView.swift:402-407) duplicate the text layout. If only the render path is updated, the selection box and drag hit area drift off the glyphs as soon as padding/max width/outline change — visible, and not covered by any existing test. Both must be driven from the same resolved style.
4. `.clipped()` on the canvas ZStack (PreviewComponentView.swift:147) plus the fixed `.frame(width:height:)` on content text layers will amputate outlines and shadows unless `inkInset` is added to the padding AND `ContentLayerCanvasGeometry.textFrameSize` grows to match. Test 20 exists specifically for this.
5. Bitmap emoji cannot be recoloured in SwiftUI, so ring-offset outlines around emoji look like offset emoji copies rather than a stroke. Accepted and documented; the acceptance criterion is no clipping, which is met. The Core Text `.strokeWidth` alternative is a trap — it requires a UIViewRepresentable, which `ImageRenderer` does not render, so export would silently lose the outline.
6. Ring outlines cost N extra `Text` layouts (8-24). At export sizes with 24 samples this measurably slows `ImageRenderer`, and macro/batch export renders many images in sequence (PremiumMakerView.swift:1218+). Keep the cap at 24 and prefer 8-12 for typical widths; if export time regresses, lower the cap rather than changing the geometry.
7. Synthesized `Codable` on `ThumbnailDocumentText` / `ThumbnailTextLayerContent` is relied on to use `decodeIfPresent`/`encodeIfPresent` for the new Optional. That is correct Swift behaviour, but test 3 must actually assert the absent `"style"` key rather than assuming it — if it ever regresses, unstyled documents would start writing `"style": null` and the "no style key" back-compat contract silently rots.
8. Do NOT repurpose the existing dead `horizontalAlignmentRawValue`/`verticalAlignmentRawValue` (ThumbnailDocument.swift:232-233) for the new alignment. They are persisted but never rendered; wiring them up would retroactively change the appearance of any old document that stored "Left" or "Top", breaking the legacy-preservation guarantee. Use the new `alignmentRawValue` inside `ThumbnailTextStyle` only.
9. Accessibility identifiers and values (`overlayTextLayer`, `textContentLayer-<id>`, `textLayerContentControls`) must stay on the same view nodes or the existing UI tests fail. The element's reported frame will grow when padding grows — the coordinate-based drag/rotate UI tests around ThumbnailMakerUITests.swift:716-790 should be re-run, not assumed.
10. A background panel materially changes text-vs-background contrast, which `ThumbnailReadinessAnalyzer` scores from `textColor` vs `backgroundColor` only. After this ships, a white-on-white title inside a black panel will still be flagged as low contrast. Deliberately out of scope; file a follow-up.
11. Pre-existing defect spotted in passing (do NOT fix here, it widens the diff): the batch-export config at PremiumMakerView.swift:1224 omits `layers:`, so macro/batch exports already drop every content layer — image, sticker, text and shape.

Consequence: a project whose colors already coincidentally match the kit will now register a real change when the kit is applied (branding gets stamped), so the "Apply brand kit" suggestion stops being a no-op and one undo entry is pushed. This is arguably correct but it IS a behaviour change in `isActionableSuggestion` (SimpleMakerViewModel.swift:816-823, PremiumMakerViewModel.swift:663-670). Mitigation: no `appliedAt` timestamp inside branding, so re-applying the SAME kit twice remains a true no-op.

- Bumping `ThumbnailDocument.currentVersion` 4 ⇒ 5 combined with `version = max(decodedVersion, Self.currentVersion)` means old drafts silently report v5 after load. That is the pre-existing convention (v4 arrived the same way) and no test hardcodes 4, but it does mean the version field cannot be used to detect "this draft predates branding" — use `branding == ThumbnailDocumentBranding()` for that if ever needed.
- Kit JSON size: `BrandKit.logoImageData` is raw `Data` and the library concatenates up to N kits into ONE file, so a library of 12 logo-bearing kits could reach several MB, all rewritten atomically on every kit edit. The `maximumKitCount = 12` cap bounds it; if logos grow, split logos into sidecar files. Worth watching in the first implementation.
- The palette-role convention (index 0 = text, 1 = background, 2 = accent) is positional and undocumented in the data model; `BrandKitEditorView.normalizedKit()` currently truncates the palette to exactly 2 entries (BrandKitEditorView.swift:183-196), which would silently destroy an accent color added elsewhere. - Library operations (create/rename/duplicate/delete a kit) are NOT part of `ThumbnailDocumentHistory` — document undo cannot bring back a deleted kit. Mitigated by `remove` returning `(kit, index)` and `restore(_:at:)` for a UI-level undo toast, but this asymmetry (document styling is undoable, library management is not) should be made explicit in the UI wording so a user does not expect Cmd-Z to resurrect a kit.
- Migration one-way-ness: after the first `saveLibrary`, the legacy `brand-kit.json` is left on disk but goes stale (it is only deleted by `delete()`). A downgraded build would silently read the stale kit. Acceptable, but the legacy file should not be treated as a live source once `brand-kits.json` exists — the load ladder must check the library file FIRST.
- `pruned(keepingLayerIDs:)` runs inside `ThumbnailDocument.init(configuration:)`, which is on the autosave hot path (called on every debounced keystroke). Keep it O(n) over a small dictionary; do not add sorting or encoding work there.

plan:
GOVERNING IDEA: the adjustment is a five-number RECIPE stored on the layer record. Pixels are never touched. `imageData` (and `configuration.selectedImage`) stay the immutable original forever, so "reset restores alpha and colour exactly" is true by construction — reset writes `nil` and the render path becomes the identity function again. Preview/export agreement is likewise structural: both rasterise the same SwiftUI view, so the only thing that can diverge is a point-valued length, which is why blur is stored normalized.

WHY COMPOSITING FILTERS, NOT A CoreImage BAKE. Baking through `CIColorControls`/`CIGaussianBlur` would (a) reintroduce a processing/memory budget on every slider tick, (b) risk halos and colour bleed on transparent cutouts because CI works premultiplied — directly against the "original alpha survives" criterion, and (c) still need blur scaled per output size. SwiftUI's `.saturation/.contrast/.brightness/.blur` are GPU compositing filters on the already-decoded layer: zero extra decode, zero extra `UIImage`, no `CIContext`. That is the honest answer to the "documented interaction/memory budgets" criterion — there is no processing stage to budget.

=== 1. NEW MODEL: ThumbnailMaker/Models/ThumbnailImageAdjustments.swift ===

```swift
struct ThumbnailImageAdjustments: Codable, Equatable, Sendable {
    static let brightnessRange: ClosedRange<Double> = -0.35...0.35   // additive, neutral 0
    static let contrastRange:   ClosedRange<Double> =  0.50...1.60   // neutral 1
    static let saturationRange: ClosedRange<Double> =  0.00...2.00   // neutral 1
    static let blurRange:       ClosedRange<Double> =  0.00...0.06   // FRACTION of rendered min side
    static let vignetteRange:   ClosedRange<Double> =  0.00...1.00   // neutral 0

    var brightness: Double = 0
    var contrast: Double = 1
    var saturation: Double = 1
    var blur: Double = 0
    var vignette: Double = 0

    static let neutral = ThumbnailImageAdjustments()
    var isNeutral: Bool { self == .neutral }
}
```

Explicit `encode(to:)` encoding all five.
- `func clamped() -> Self`: each field `min(hi, max(lo, v))`, and FIRST replace non-finite values (`!v.isFinite`) with the neutral default — `Double` decodes NaN from a hand-edited file and NaN would poison `==`, `isNeutral`, and every SwiftUI modifier.

- `func blurRadius(forRenderedSize size: CGSize) -> CGFloat` → `blur <= 0 ? 0 : CGFloat(blur) * min(size.width, size.height)`. **This is the preview/export parity mechanism** — the same recipe yields 1.4pt of blur on a 350x197 canvas and 51.2pt on a 1280x720 export, i.e. the same picture.

```swift
struct ThumbnailAdjustmentsModifier: ViewModifier {
    let adjustments: ThumbnailImageAdjustments?
    let renderedSize: CGSize
    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
```

4. EXPORT CORRECTNESS DEPENDS ON A SYNCHRONOUS RESOLVER. `ThumbnailExporter.render` runs `ImageRenderer` over the live SwiftUI tree in one synchronous pass. If an implementer "improves" `ContentImageLayerCanvasItem` by resolving the masked image asynchronously (`.task`, `@StateObject`, a Combine publisher), EXPORTS WILL SILENTLY SHIP THE UNMASKED IMAGE while the on-screen preview looks correct. The resolver must stay synchronous and always native-resolution on the canvas; only the refinement sheet's live drag uses previewMaxDimension.

5. CIGaussianBlur EXTENT GROWTH. Feathering without `clampedToExtent()` before the blur and `.cropped(to:)` after it erodes and darkens the mask border, which shows up as a halo around the whole image. Test 15 exists specifically to catch this.

6. blendWithMask SEMANTICS. `CIFilter.blendWithMask` must be used with a CLEAR background image so result alpha = sourceAlpha * maskLuma. Using an opaque background, or writing the mask straight into the alpha channel, REPLACES rather than multiplies and destroys pre-existing partial alpha — which is exactly the acceptance criterion the feature exists to satisfy. Tests 13 and 11 pin it.

7. MEMORY. A cached full-resolution RGBA composite of a 12 MP photo is ~48 MB. The NSCache needs an explicit totalCostLimit and a memory-warning purge, or Mac Catalyst / older iPads will get jetsammed with several masked layers open.

8. HISTORY COST PER STROKE. `ThumbnailDocument` snapshots share `Data` buffers by COW, so per-stroke history entries do NOT copy image bytes — but `ThumbnailDocumentHistory.record` compares whole documents for equality, which memcmps the image Data every time. Commit strokes on gesture END only, and prefer one history entry per refinement session (the sheet's local undo stack handles per-stroke undo). Per-touch-sample commits would make brushing visibly janky on large photos.

9. FINGERPRINT MUST NOT HASH IMAGE BYTES. The cache key is recomputed on every render pass. `ThumbnailCutoutMask.fingerprint` must be O(strokes) and use the automatic base's pre-assigned `id`, never a SHA over the mask or source PNG — hashing a 10 MB payload per frame would be far worse than the decode it replaces.

10. NORMALIZED-SPACE AMBIGUITY. Vision's `normalizedBounds` are bottom-left origin (see BackgroundRemovalService.croppedImage's `1 - clampedRect.maxY` flip at :138). ThumbnailCutoutPoint is deliberately TOP-LEFT origin to match CoreGraphics image space and the SwiftUI canvas. Mixing the two conventions flips masks vertically. Document it on the type and assert it in test 11 by erasing an asymmetric region.

11. RADIUS NORMALIZATION BASIS. Radius/feather are normalized to the image's LONG side, not to width, height or the canvas. Any other basis makes a brush change size when a portrait image is swapped for a landscape one and breaks resolution independence.

12. `ThumbnailSubjectProcessing` GROWS. Adding `foregroundAlphaMask` without a protocol-extension default would break `StubSubjectProcessor` (ThumbnailMakerTests.swift:2880) and force a second edit to that already-contended file. The default implementation is not optional polish; it is what keeps the test file out of Slice B's blast radius for the protocol change.

13. BASE-IMAGE MASK CANNOT BE FINGERPRINTED BY BYTES. `SimpleMakerConfigurationModel.selectedImage` is a decoded UIImage that ThumbnailDocument re-encodes to PNG on every round trip (ThumbnailDocument.swift:1385-1397), so its bytes are not stable. That is why `ThumbnailCutoutAutomaticBase` carries `sourcePixelWidth/Height` for staleness rather than a content hash, and why the revision counter is the primary guard.

14. VISION AVAILABILITY IS A NON-ISSUE BUT THE FALLBACK MATTERS. Deployment target is iOS 18.1, so `supportsForegroundMask` is always true. Still, `automaticBase == nil` must be a first-class state: brush-only refinement on an image with no auto cutout has to work, and it is also the state a user lands in after Reset.

15. SCOPE CREEP. The backlog mentions optional subject outline/shadow. That is a separate renderer concern (a dilated, offset copy of the resolved mask) and should NOT be attempted in this feature; it would widen the model, the sheet and the export path. Ship mask + brush + feather first.

plan:
Goal: a short, optional, resumable first-export guide that runs as an inline checklist card over the real editor features. The guide never changes the document by itself; every step is satisfied by watching real editor state, and anything it launches is a normal, undoable action through the existing editor paths. People who ignore the guide and export directly also complete it, silently.

KEY DESIGN DECISIONS
1. Guide state is app-level, not document-level.
   - It lives in its own small JSON store, following the BrandKitStore pattern: Application Support/ThumbnailMaker/Guide/first-export-guide.json.
   - ThumbnailDocument and ThumbnailProjectMetadata are left untouched, so wave 2 (portable project files, personal templates, brand kits, photo adjustments) cannot conflict, and project files never carry onboarding state.
   - Every field decodes with decodeIfPresent and a default, plus a schemaVersion. A file from a newer app, or an unreadable file, is treated as "dismissed" and never shown.
2. Steps are derived, not scripted. A pure function maps an editor snapshot to the set of satisfied steps, so starting the guide on existing work shows it as already done and nothing is ever reset. The steps are:
   - addVisual: a background image or any content layer. "Show me" opens the real PhotosPicker bound to viewModel.imageSelection. A secondary "Use a template" opens the existing templatesButton sheet, which will include wave-2 personal templates automatically.
   - writeTitle: trimmed overlay text is not empty, or any text layer exists. "Show me" focuses the existing OverlayTextEditor through the existing @FocusState.
   - checkReadiness: ThumbnailReadinessAnalyzer.analyze(config) has been viewed and a size check has run, i.e. exportReport is not nil after an explicit check. "Show me" calls the existing checkExportSize(). Readiness warnings are advisory and do not block the step. The card shows the real displayScore; it invents no copy or evidence.
   - export: set only by a confirmed export event (Photos saved, Files export succeeded, or share activity completed=true). The card shows the three real export actions by calling the view's existing saveImage / prepareFileExport / shareImage functions.
   - An optional hint for Brand Kit points at the existing brandKitButton sheet. It does not count as a step, so the guide stays short (4 steps).
3. Status machine: notStarted -> active -> (paused | skipped | completed).
   - paused ("Hide for now") keeps currentStep and completedSteps and can be resumed from Settings or from the card's collapsed pill.
   - skipped hides the guide permanently until "Show first-export guide" in Settings.
   - completed is set by the first confirmed export in either editor, even while notStarted, skipped or paused. That is the direct journey: no nagging afterwards.
   - "Restart guide" clears guide progress only. It never touches projects or the document.
   - The optional "Start in a new project" button is shown only when isProjectLibraryAvailable. It calls the existing createNewProject(), which commits the current project first, so earlier work stays in the library. It is never automatic.
4. The guide is shown only for a true first run: status == notStarted and the editor has no exportable content at launch. Existing users (content, or a restored draft) get no card and no prompt; the guide is reachable from Settings. Under UI tests (-DisableDraftPersistence) the store is in-memory and starts as .dismissedForTests unless -UITestFirstExportGuide is passed, so existing UI tests stay unchanged.

NEW FILES
A. ThumbnailMaker/Models/FirstExportGuide.swift
   - enum FirstExportGuideStep: String, Codable, CaseIterable { addVisual, writeTitle, checkReadiness, export }, with title/detail strings.
   - enum FirstExportGuideStatus: String, Codable { notStarted, active, paused, skipped, completed }.
   - enum ThumbnailExportEventKind: String, Codable { photos, files, share }.
   - struct ThumbnailExportEvent: Equatable, Identifiable { id: UUID; kind; date; editorMode: ThumbnailDocumentEditorMode }.
   - struct FirstExportGuideProgress: Codable, Equatable. Fields: schemaVersion = 1; status; currentStep?; completedSteps: [FirstExportGuideStep]; startedAt?, pausedAt?, skippedAt?, completedAt?; firstExportKind?; lastEditorMode?. It has a custom init(from:) using decodeIfPresent throughout, and isSupported = schemaVersion <= current.
   - struct FirstExportGuideSnapshot: Equatable. Fields: hasVisual, hasTitle, hasSizeCheck, readinessScore, readinessHasWarnings, hasExportableContent. It has static factories make(simple: SimpleMakerConfigurationModel, exportReport:) and make(premium: PremiumMakerConfigurationModel, exportReport:). Both use ThumbnailReadinessConfiguration and layers.hasContentLayers, so no view-model internals are involved.
   - enum FirstExportGuideReducer, with pure static functions:
     - satisfiedSteps(snapshot, exported: Bool) -> Set<Step>
     - nextStep(satisfied) -> Step?
     - reduce(progress, action) -> progress, where action is one of start(now), pause(now), resume(now), skip(now), restart, observe(snapshot), exportSucceeded(event).
     - shouldOfferOnLaunch(progress, snapshot) -> Bool
   - Invariant: reduce never drops a completed step through observe. Steps are monotonic once the export is done, but earlier steps may re-open while active if the user deletes content; the export step stays done.
B. ThumbnailMaker/Services/FirstExportGuideStore.swift
   - A final class with fileURL injection like BrandKitStore, plus an .inMemory variant for tests.
   - load() -> FirstExportGuideProgress: a missing file gives .init(); a corrupt or unsupported file gives status .skipped and the file is left untouched.
   - save(_:) writes atomically.
   - static func forLaunch(arguments:) handles -DisableDraftPersistence, -UITestFirstExportGuide and -UITestResetFirstExportGuide.
C. ThumbnailMaker/ViewModels/FirstExportGuideController.swift
   - @MainActor final class, ObservableObject, with `static let shared`.
   - @Published private(set) progress and @Published private(set) isCardVisible.
   - Methods: offerIfFirstRun(snapshot:), start(), pause(), resume(), skip(), restart(), observe(_ snapshot:), recordExport(_ event:).
   - Each mutation runs reduce and then store.save. A save failure is swallowed into an in-memory state; the guide never shows an alert.
   - The injected clock and store keep it unit-testable.
   - It is shared by both editors, so a first export in Premium completes the guide in Simple as well.
D. ThumbnailMaker/Views/Components/FirstExportGuideCard.swift
   - A SwiftUI inline card (not a sheet or overlay, so it never covers the canvas or blocks existing controls). It takes progress, snapshot and a FirstExportGuideActions struct of closures: pickImage (PhotosPicker binding passed in), openTemplates, focusTitle, checkSize, saveToPhotos, exportToFiles, share, startNewProject?.
   - It shows "Step n of 4", a checklist with checkmarks, a single "Show me" primary button, and "Hide for now" / "Skip guide" buttons.
   - Collapsed paused state: a small "Resume guide" pill.
   - Completed state: a one-time "First export done" row with a Dismiss button.
   - Supports Dynamic Type and VoiceOver: combined elements, and step status in accessibilityValue.
   - Accessibility identifiers: firstExportGuideCard, firstExportGuideStep-<rawValue>, firstExportGuideShowMeButton, firstExportGuideHideButton, firstExportGuideSkipButton, firstExportGuideResumeButton, firstExportGuideCompletedRow, firstExportGuideDismissButton, firstExportGuideNewProjectButton, firstExportGuideTemplatesButton.
E. ThumbnailMaker/Views/Components/FirstExportGuideSettingsRow.swift
   - A Section "Getting Started" with a "Show first-export guide" button (calls resume or restart) and a status label.
   - Identifiers: firstExportGuideSettingsButton, firstExportGuideSettingsStatus.

MODIFIED FILES (narrow hooks only)
1. ThumbnailMaker/ViewModels/SimpleMakerViewModel.swift, about 8 lines.
   - Add `@Published private(set) var lastExportEvent: ThumbnailExportEvent?`.
   - Set it in the success branches of saveImageWithOverlay (around line 1004), in handleFileExportCompletion .success (around line 1124), and in a new `func recordShareCompleted(_ completed: Bool)`, which sets .share only when completed is true.
   - checkExportSize is not changed.
2. ThumbnailMaker/ViewModels/PremiumMakerViewModel.swift, the same small hooks: saveImageWithOverlay success around line 852, handleFileExportCompletion around line 977, and recordShareCompleted.
3. ThumbnailMaker/Views/Components/ShareSheet.swift
   - Add `var onComplete: ((Bool) -> Void)? = nil` and wire completionWithItemsHandler.
   - The default nil keeps every existing call site source-compatible.
4. ThumbnailMaker/Views/Main/SimpleMakerView.swift, about 25 lines.
   - Add `@ObservedObject private var guide = FirstExportGuideController.shared`.
   - Add a `firstExportGuideSection` computed view, inserted first in the compact VStack (before variantBarSection, around line 225) and first in the right pane of the regular layout (around line 271). It builds the snapshot and actions from the existing private funcs saveImage, prepareFileExport, shareImage and checkExportSize, the isFocused state, isTemplateGalleryPresented, and viewModel.createNewProject.
   - Add `.onChange(of: viewModel.simpleMakerConfiguration)` / `.onChange(of: viewModel.exportReport)` to call guide.observe.
   - Add `.onChange(of: viewModel.lastExportEvent)` to call guide.recordExport.
   - Add `.task { guide.offerIfFirstRun(...) }`.
   - Pass onComplete: viewModel.recordShareCompleted to the ShareSheet at line 157.
   - The card uses its own PhotosPicker bound to $viewModel.imageSelection, so image import follows the existing onChange at line 165 and its undo path.
5. ThumbnailMaker/Views/Main/PremiumMakerView.swift
   - Slice 1: only the ShareSheet onComplete and the lastExportEvent → guide.recordExport onChange, so direct exports in Premium complete the guide.
   - Slice 2 (optional): the same card, placed with the same pattern.
6. ThumbnailMaker/Views/Main/SettingsView.swift: insert FirstExportGuideSettingsRow() as a new Section after "About" (line 21).
No changes to ThumbnailDocument, ThumbnailProjectMetadata, ThumbnailProjectLibrary, the templates, the brand kit or the export code. This composes with wave 2 because the guide calls the existing sheets and buttons that wave 2 extends.

MOST VALUABLE END-TO-END SLICE (if time-boxed): A, B, C, D, the Simple Maker hooks, the SimpleMakerViewModel event hooks, ShareSheet onComplete, and the Settings row. Premium gets only the export-event completion hook. The Premium card is deferred.

risks:
1. Share completion is only observable through the UIActivityViewController completionWithItemsHandler. Simulator UI tests cannot reliably pick an activity, so the UI test only asserts the export step is reached, and completion is covered by unit tests. Do not add a fake "simulate export" launch argument, because that would amount to invented evidence.
2. exportReport is also set by checkExportSize. Completion must use the new lastExportEvent, never exportReport. A unit test guards this.
3. The existing UI tests all launch with -DisableDraftPersistence. The guide must default to hidden in that mode, otherwise the inserted card shifts layout, which can break coordinate- or hittability-based tests such as the edge-handle and large Dynamic Type tests.
4. Wave 2 is concurrently editing SimpleMakerView, PremiumMakerView, the view models and SettingsView, so merge conflicts are likely. Keep the hooks small and in separate, clearly marked `// FEATURE-13` blocks. Do not touch ThumbnailDocument or ThumbnailProjectMetadata, which wave 2 (portable files, templates) is likely to change.
5. Premium saveImageWithOverlay consumes a free trial (PurchaseManager.useFreeTrial). The guide must never trigger Premium exports automatically; it only relays user taps. This is why Slice 1 limits Premium to the completion hook.
6. The guide card's PhotosPicker shares viewModel.imageSelection with the main picker. Both route through the existing updateImage and its undo history, so there is no reset, but replacing an existing background image is still possible if the user picks one. The addVisual step is already done whenever an image exists, so "Show me" for it only appears on empty canvases.
7. "Start in a new project" depends on the FEATURE-01 library being available. It is hidden when projectLibrary is nil, as in UI-test mode.
8. The copy must not claim study-based effectiveness. Keep the strings factual and step-oriented.

5. Services/ThumbnailExportQueueRunner.swift
@MainActor final class ThumbnailExportQueueRunner: ObservableObject.
- Published: jobStates [JobID: JobState], where JobState is pending, running, succeeded(Outcome{fileName, url?, bytes, quality, qualityReduced}), failed(String), skipped(String) or notRun.
- Also published: isRunning, completedCount, totalCount, progress.
- Protocols:
  - ThumbnailExportJobRendering: `@MainActor func render(_ document:, size:) throws -> UIImage`.
  - ThumbnailExportDestinationWriting: `snapshot() throws -> Snapshot`, `func write(_ data:, fileName:, format:, policy:) async throws -> WriteResult`.
- run(plan) processes jobs sequentially in an autoreleasepool:
  1. Render on the main actor through ThumbnailExporter.render using ThumbnailExportOptions(usesCustomSize: true, customSize: size, format, quality). This reuses the existing exporter.
  2. Encode and fit in a detached utility task, calling ThumbnailExporter.encodedData(for:options:) with the quality overridden.
  3. Write.
  4. Update state.
- A job error marks that job failed and the queue continues (partial failure).
- cancel() cancels the Task. The in-flight write is atomic. Remaining jobs become notRun.
- retryFailed() re-plans against a fresh destination snapshot (conflicts are recomputed) and runs only failed and notRun jobs. Succeeded and skipped jobs are never re-rendered.

risks:
1. Memory and time. Nine full-res renders (3840x2160 through SwiftUI ImageRenderer on the main actor) are heavy. Mitigations: run strictly sequentially, use an autoreleasepool per job, release the UIImage before writing, and encode off the main thread. The UI can stutter during each render, so show progress and do not claim it runs in the background.
2. Render parity. The queue renders from ThumbnailDocument.makeSimple/PremiumConfiguration(), not the live binding. Any field that is not round-tripped in the document (for example transient editor state) would differ from the single export. The parity pixel test guards this. Wave-2 photo adjustments and brand kits must be persisted in the document to appear.
3. Aspect handling. The existing single export lets custom sizes of any ratio through. The queue blocks mismatches instead, and users may expect it to crop. The block reason must be clear, with a hint to "duplicate variant and change the canvas ratio".
4. Security-scoped folder access. Bookmarks can go stale, and iCloud Drive folders may be slow or offline. Re-snapshot before Run and before Retry, and surface a stale-bookmark error so the user re-picks the folder. The Photos destination cannot honor names or overwrite, and the UI must say so explicitly.
5. The fitter's binary search assumes quality versus bytes is roughly monotonic. WebP and HEIC-backed encoders can be non-monotonic, so always verify the final bytes against the budget, never an estimate.
6. Concurrent wave-2 edits to SimpleMakerView, PremiumMakerView and ThumbnailVariantBarView could conflict. The hooks are about 10 lines each and additive, and the default-nil closure keeps other callers compiling.
7. The recipe store is a new app-level file. If wave 2's portable project files want recipes inside projects, embed ThumbnailExportRecipe as an optional field later rather than duplicating the model.
8. Cancel is cooperative. A render that is already running on the main actor cannot be interrupted, so cancel takes effect at the next job or fitter-attempt boundary. The UI should show "Cancelling…".
