plan:
GOAL (end-to-end slice)
From either editor, open "Series". The user freezes the current design (or a FEATURE-05 personal template) as an IMMUTABLE source. They then edit a table of up to 100 rows (title, episode, image, slot, optional output name) or import a documented CSV. Each row is validated and previewed on its own. The user renders every valid row deterministically through a cancellable, retryable queue, then saves the results to Photos or shares them as files. The acceptance fixture is a 10-row CSV with 3 malformed rows: 7 rows render and the 3 bad ones are isolated with line-numbered errors.

1. MODEL (pure value types, Codable, all fields added after v1 are optional/decodeIfPresent)
Models/ThumbnailSeries.swift
- struct ThumbnailSeries: Codable, Equatable
  - Fields: version=1, id UUID, name, createdAt, updatedAt, editorMode, source: ThumbnailSeriesSource, rows: [ThumbnailSeriesRow], exportOptionsOverride: ThumbnailDocumentExport? (nil means use the source's export).
  - Custom init(from:) uses decodeIfPresent for everything except id, source and rows, following the ThumbnailDocument.init(from:) pattern at Models/ThumbnailDocument.swift:199.
  - Static rowLimit = 100, mirroring MacroConfig's <100.
- struct ThumbnailSeriesSource: Codable, Equatable (IMMUTABLE)
  - Fields: capturedAt, origin: ThumbnailSeriesSourceOrigin, defaultSlot, documents: [ThumbnailVariantSlot: ThumbnailDocument] (stored dehydrated, see store), digest: String.
  - digest is SHA256 over the sorted-keys JSON of the documents with updatedAt zeroed, like ThumbnailDocumentHistory.snapshot.
  - Only `let` properties and no mutating API. The only way to change a series' source is ThumbnailSeries.replacingSource(_:), an explicit user action ("Re-capture from current design") that returns a new series and marks every row's render state stale.
- enum ThumbnailSeriesSourceOrigin: Codable
  - Cases: .project(id: UUID, name: String), .personalTemplate(id: String, name: String), .unknown.
  - The .personalTemplate case is how FEATURE-05 composes. Series only needs a ThumbnailDocument, so it takes `ThumbnailSeriesSource.capture(documents:origin:defaultSlot:)` and never imports FEATURE-05 types. Unknown origin raw values decode to .unknown.
- struct ThumbnailSeriesRow: Codable, Equatable, Identifiable
  - Fields: id UUID, title String, episode String?, imageRef: ThumbnailSeriesImageRef?, slot: ThumbnailVariantSlot? (nil means source.defaultSlot), outputName String?, imageRecipe: ThumbnailImageFrameRecipe? (nil means the source's fit mode, centered, zoom 1), sourceLine Int? (CSV line, for diagnostics).
- struct ThumbnailSeriesImageRef: Codable, Equatable
  - Fields: digest String, originalFileName String.
- Render state is NOT persisted in the row, which keeps rows reversible and pure. It lives in the queue (below). The only persisted result is renders: [UUID: ThumbnailSeriesRenderRecord]? on ThumbnailSeries (optional). A record holds documentDigest, sourceDigest, fileName and renderedAt. It is used to show "rendered, up to date" and becomes stale when either digest changes.

Models/ThumbnailSeriesRecipe.swift (the deterministic, reversible core)
- enum ThumbnailSeriesRecipe with static func document(for row:, in source:, imageData: (String)->Data?) -> Result<ThumbnailDocument, ThumbnailSeriesRowError>. It is a pure function of (source, row, asset bytes):
  a) Pick base = source.documents[row.slot ?? source.defaultSlot], else .slotMissing(slot).
  b) Tokens: `{title}` and `{episode}` are replaced in text.value and in every .text content layer, via layers.updateTextContent (Models/ThumbnailDocument.swift:1020). If no `{title}` token exists anywhere, title replaces text.value (the primary title).
  c) Image: when imageRef is set, imageData = asset bytes and imageRecipe = row.imageRecipe ?? source recipe.with(fit:) re-centered with zoom 1. A focus/zoom tuned for another photo is not reused. Any wave-2 photo-adjustment fields on the document are copied untouched, since series never reads them.
  d) updatedAt = source.capturedAt (fixed, so the output is deterministic). version is unchanged.
  e) The layers are re-reconciled exactly as the configuration initialisers do.
- The source is never mutated; the function returns a copy.
- static func documentDigest(_ doc:) is used by the render record and by the tests.

Models/ThumbnailSeriesValidation.swift
- enum ThumbnailSeriesRowError: Equatable, LocalizedError. Cases: emptyTitle, titleTooLong(max 100), slotMissing(slot), unknownSlot(String), imageNotImported(fileName), imageUnreadable, duplicateOutputName(name), malformedCSV(line, reason).
- struct ThumbnailSeriesRowIssue: severity (.error blocks rendering, .warning does not), message.
- ThumbnailSeriesValidator.validate(series:assets:) -> [UUID: [ThumbnailSeriesRowIssue]]
  - Errors come from the list above.
  - Warnings: an episode is present but the chosen slot document has no `{episode}` token ("episode will not appear"). Also any ThumbnailReadinessAnalyzer warnings for the recipe's document, run through makeSimpleConfiguration()/makePremiumConfiguration() by editorMode. Examples are text density over 64 chars and low contrast.
  - Output names are made unique after sanitising: ThumbnailVariantExportNaming.sanitized(outputName ?? "\(seriesName)-\(episode ?? index)"). Duplicates are a per-row error on the later rows only.

Models/ThumbnailSeriesCSV.swift (documented, tolerant, per-record isolation)
- ThumbnailSeriesCSVParser.parse(_ data: Data) -> ThumbnailSeriesCSVResult. The result holds rows [(line: Int, fields: [String: String])], rowErrors [(line, ThumbnailSeriesRowError)] and fileError: FileError? (notUTF8, empty, missingHeader, missingTitleColumn, duplicateHeader(name), tooManyRows(limit)).
- Format: UTF-8 with an optional BOM; comma delimiter; RFC 4180 quoting (`""` escape, newlines inside quotes); CRLF, LF or CR line endings; blank lines skipped.
- The header row is required. Headers are case- and whitespace-insensitive: title (required), episode, image, slot, name. Unknown columns are ignored and reported once as a file-level warning.
- Malformed records are isolated: a field-count mismatch, an unterminated quote (resynchronised at the next unquoted line start) or an invalid slot value records an error for that line and parsing continues.
- ThumbnailSeriesCSVImporter.rows(from: result, importedImages: [fileName: digest]) maps records to ThumbnailSeriesRow. The image cell is matched case-insensitively against the originalFileName of images the user imported into the series, and an unmatched name becomes an .imageNotImported row issue (the row is kept, not dropped). A malformed record becomes a placeholder row carrying sourceLine and the error, so the user sees and fixes it in place.
- Inverse ThumbnailSeriesCSVWriter.csv(for rows) gives "Export table as CSV" and a round-trip test.

Models/ThumbnailSeriesRowsHistory.swift
- A small undo/redo for table edits (stacks of [ThumbnailSeriesRow], limit 20). It uses the same record/undo/redo semantics as ThumbnailDocumentHistory (Models/ThumbnailDocumentHistory.swift:8-60).
- Series edits never enter the editor's document history, so they cannot cross the FEATURE-02 per-variant stacks.

2. PERSISTENCE
Services/ThumbnailSeriesStore.swift
- A file-backed store in the project directory: projectDirectory(id)/series/<seriesID>/series.json, plus series/<seriesID>/assets/<sha256>.png and series/<seriesID>/renders/<fileName>.<ext>.
- Source documents and row images are dehydrated into assets with ThumbnailVariantAssetLibrary.dehydrate/hydrate (Services/ThumbnailVariantAssetLibrary.swift:55/94), so each image is stored once.
- API: list() -> [ThumbnailSeriesSummary], load(id), save(series) (atomic write), importImage(data, originalFileName) -> ThumbnailSeriesImageRef (normalises to PNG like ThumbnailDocument.encodedImageData), assetData(digest), writeRender(data, fileName), renderURL(fileName), delete(id).
- An unreadable series.json is quarantined and reported, following ThumbnailProjectStore.quarantineIndex (Services/ThumbnailProjectStore.swift:98). It never crashes and never silently drops data.
- Because the store lives under the project directory, project purge removes it and trash keeps it. Project duplicate does not copy it, since copyProjectFiles (Services/ThumbnailProjectStore.swift:174) copies only document + preview, matching today's variant behaviour. This is documented and noted as a follow-up.
- A static factory ThumbnailSeriesStore(projectDirectory:) takes an injected root for tests.

3. RENDER QUEUE
Services/ThumbnailSeriesRenderer.swift
- protocol ThumbnailSeriesRendering { @MainActor func render(_ document: ThumbnailDocument, options: ThumbnailExportOptions) throws -> Data }.
- The live implementation builds the same content as ThumbnailProjectPreviewRenderer: PreviewComponentView or PremiumPreviewComponentView with isInteractive:false at options.outputSize, then ThumbnailExporter.render + encodedData. It never touches a view model's live configuration, which is what fixes the macro batch's mutation of overlayText.
- A fake renderer is used in tests.

ViewModels/ThumbnailSeriesQueue.swift (@MainActor final class, ObservableObject)
- Published items: [ThumbnailSeriesJob]. A job holds rowID and state: .pending | .rendering | .done(fileName) | .failed(message) | .skipped(issue) | .cancelled.
- start(series, assets): rows with error issues become .skipped and are never rendered. Rows are processed one at a time in table order inside a single Task; a failing row becomes .failed and the queue continues.
- cancel(): Task cancellation is checked before each row, the current row finishes atomically, and the remaining rows become .cancelled.
- retryFailed() re-queues only .failed and .cancelled rows. retry(rowID) handles a single row.
- On success the queue writes the render record (documentDigest + sourceDigest) through the store. A re-run skips rows whose record matches the current digests ("up to date") unless forced.
- progress = done / renderable. There is no Task.sleep throttle.

4. SERIES VIEW MODEL + UI (all new files)
ViewModels/ThumbnailSeriesViewModel.swift (@MainActor ObservableObject)
- Initialised with (store, source: ThumbnailSeriesSource, projectName, editorMode, renderer).
- Holds the series, the rowsHistory, validation issues (recomputed on each rows change) and the queue.
- Intents: addRow, updateRow, deleteRows, moveRows, undo/redo, importCSV(Data), exportCSV(), importImages([ (Data, name) ]), setImage(rowID, data, name), recaptureSource(_:) (with confirmation), render(), cancel(), retryFailed(), saveAllToPhotos() (ThumbnailExporter.saveEncodedDataToPhotoLibrary), shareURLs().
- Previews are lazy per-row thumbnails at 320px through ThumbnailProjectPreviewRenderer.previewPNGData(for: recipeDocument), cached by documentDigest.

Views/Series/ThumbnailSeriesView.swift
- A NavigationStack sheet. Header: source card (thumbnail, origin, captured date, "Immutable source" badge, Re-capture button). Then the row List (ThumbnailSeriesRowView) with a toolbar for Import CSV (fileImporter [.commaSeparatedText, .plainText]), Import images (PhotosPicker, multi), Add row, Export CSV, and Undo/Redo via the existing UndoRedoToolbarButtons. Bottom bar: Render / Cancel / Retry failed / Save to Photos / Share.
Views/Series/ThumbnailSeriesRowView.swift
- Inline title/episode fields, slot picker (only slots present in the source), image chip, status and issue badges, small preview.
Views/Series/ThumbnailSeriesCSVHelpView.swift
- In-app copy of the CSV format with a "Copy sample CSV" button.
Views/Series/ThumbnailSeriesQueueBar.swift
- Progress plus counts (done / failed / skipped / cancelled). It generalises the look of BatchProgressView without changing that file.

5. NARROW HOOKS IN EXISTING FILES
- ViewModels/SimpleMakerViewModel.swift and PremiumMakerViewModel.swift: one small `// FEATURE-15` extension each, about 15 lines. It adds `func makeSeriesSource() -> ThumbnailSeriesSource?`, which commits the live edit (commitEditorStateNow) and captures liveVariantSet documents, activeSlot/preferredSlot as defaultSlot, and origin .project(activeProjectID, activeProjectName). It also adds `var seriesStore: ThumbnailSeriesStore?`, built from projectLibrary.store.projectDirectory(id: activeProjectID), and `var isSeriesAvailable: Bool`. Premium additionally blocks opening Series while isBatchGenerating. No existing function bodies change.
- Views/Main/SimpleMakerView.swift and PremiumMakerView.swift: one toolbar Button in the existing trailing ToolbarItemGroup (next to templatesButton, SimpleMakerView.swift:63-70 / PremiumMakerView.swift:182-190) with accessibilityIdentifier "seriesButton" and SF symbol "rectangle.stack.badge.plus". Also one `.sheet(isPresented: $isSeriesPresented) { ThumbnailSeriesView(...) }` and one @State. About 20 lines each.
- Entitlement: authoring, validation and previews are free. Render/export is gated by purchaseManager.canAccessPremium, consistent with the "Batch generate thumbnails for video series" premium bullet (Views/Main/SettingsView.swift:37). The gate is passed as a Bool into ThumbnailSeriesView.
- FEATURE-05 compose point: when the personal-template store exists, ThumbnailSeriesView's source card offers "Use personal template…", which calls ThumbnailSeriesSource.capture(documents:[slot: template.document], origin: .personalTemplate(...)). Series defines no template storage of its own.
- FEATURE-06 portable project files: series lives under the project directory in its own subfolder, so the package writer can include `series/` verbatim. Assets are content-addressed and every field is optional, so no schema coupling is needed.
- Brand kits: not applied by series. Whatever the source captured is frozen, which avoids duplicating brand-kit logic.

6. DOCS
docs/SERIES_CSV.md: columns, quoting, encoding, limits, the image-matching rule, token rules ({title}/{episode}), slot semantics, error catalogue and a sample, with a sample file at ThumbnailMakerTests/Fixtures/series-10-rows.csv.

Out of scope for this slice: pulling titles from YouTube, per-row text restyling, background execution and project-duplicate copying of series.

risks:
1. Rendering determinism depends on SwiftUI ImageRenderer. It is deterministic on the same device and OS at scale 1, but byte equality across OS versions is not guaranteed. The tests should assert document-digest determinism as the contract and pixel equality only within one run.
2. ImageRenderer is @MainActor. Rendering 100 rows at 1280x720 in sequence can hitch the UI and hold memory, so the plan renders one row at a time, drops UIImage references after encoding, writes to disk immediately and yields between rows with Task.yield instead of sleeping. There is no background execution: leaving the sheet cancels the queue.
3. Concurrent wave-2 overlap:
   - FEATURE-05 personal templates: only an origin enum case and a capture() entry point, with no type dependency.
   - FEATURE-06 portable files: the series/ subfolder must be included by that packer, so coordinate the folder name.
   - Brand kits: not applied.
   - Photo adjustments: carried over from the source document untouched. If FEATURE-08 stores adjustments keyed to the image, a per-row image might need its own adjustments, so that is a follow-up.
   Merge conflicts are likely only in the two main views' toolbar group and the view-model tail extensions. Keep the hooks in clearly marked blocks.
4. The Premium entitlement decision (gate render and export, keep authoring free) needs product sign-off. The existing macro batch stays as it is, and the two batch features coexist. Opening Series is blocked during macro batch generation.
5. Reusing the source frame recipe for a different photo is ambiguous, so the policy resets focus/zoom and keeps the fit mode. Users may expect the crop to carry over, which the per-row override addresses.
6. Series is not copied on project duplicate, because copyProjectFiles copies only document+preview. This is an existing limitation that also affects variants, and it is documented.
7. The CSV fixture resource may need the test target's synchronized-group membership. Fall back to an inline string if needed.
8. Tokens `{title}`/`{episode}` are ordinary characters in existing designs. A design that already contains literal "{title}" would be substituted, which is an acceptable and documented edge case.

plan:
RECOMMENDED SLICE (build this first, end to end in both editors)
The slice covers multi-selection, group and ungroup, moving a selection or group (drag, arrow keys, numeric), align and distribute, snapping to visible objects with an off switch, and workspace zoom, pan and fit. Group scale and rotate by number are phase B, built on the same engine. Direct-manipulation handles for resizing or rotating a whole group are phase C.

KEY DESIGN DECISIONS
1. Groups store membership only; transforms are baked in. Each layer gets an optional `groupID: String?`. No group-level transform is ever stored. A group operation writes the members' own transform, size, width and height right away. Consequences:
   - Ungroup only clears groupID, so appearance is unchanged by construction.
   - Export, readiness, templates, variants and the wave-2 portable files need no change to render groups.
   - Undo works through the existing whole-document snapshots in ThumbnailDocumentHistory.
   - Grouping does not reorder z. Members keep their zIndex so appearance stays the same, and the layer strip shows a group badge.
2. Codable stays back-compatible with no version bump. ThumbnailDocumentLayer gains `var groupID: String? = nil`. Its Codable is synthesized, so an optional decodes with decodeIfPresent. Old v5 JSON decodes with groupID nil, and nil is omitted on encode. `currentVersion` stays 5 so it cannot collide with wave-2 bumps; wave 2 owns any bump.
3. Selection is UI state, not document state and not undoable, just like today's `selectedLayer`. It is the value type `ThumbnailSelectionSet`, holding ordered members plus a primary. The existing `selectedLayer` stays the primary, so every current single-selection code path (text controls, remove background, and so on) keeps working unchanged.
4. Workspace geometry is kept separate from export geometry. `ThumbnailWorkspaceViewport` (zoom and fit mode) is @State or @SceneStorage in the Main view. `CanvasWorkspaceView` wraps only the interactive preview: a two-axis ScrollView holding a `.frame(width*zoom, height*zoom)` with `.scaleEffect(zoom, anchor: .topLeading)` applied to the unchanged preview. The preview still gets the real canvas width and height. Export call sites never pass through the workspace. A unit test and a UI test prove the exported PNG is byte-identical at zoom 1 and zoom 3.
5. Rules for locked and hidden layers:
   - The background is never selectable.
   - Hidden layers cannot be picked on the canvas. They can be picked in the strip, but are excluded from align, distribute, snap targets and selection bounds.
   - Locked layers can be selected and inspected. They are skipped by every move, align, distribute, scale and rotate, and still act as snap targets and as the "key object" reference.
   - A group with any locked member cannot be transformed. Commands return `.skipped(reason: .containsLocked)`, which is announced through VoiceOver and shown inline.
   - Hidden group members move with their group so relative layout is kept, but they do not count toward bounds.
6. Groups act as one unit. Selecting any member expands the selection to the whole group, unless "edit inside group" is on. Align and distribute treat each group as a single item using its union bounds.

risks:
1. Gesture coordinates under zoom. Gestures inside the preview are assumed to report translation in the unscaled local space when scaleEffect is applied outside. The named coordinate space is declared inside the preview, which should make this work, but it must be checked early with a UI test at 2x zoom. Fallback: divide translation by the zoom carried in CanvasArrangementContext.
2. Pinch conflicts. The workspace MagnifyGesture could clash with the content RotationGesture and the ScrollView pan. Keep pinch on the background only and give the zoom buttons and shortcuts as the reliable path.
3. Bounds are estimates. Text bounds use ContentLayerCanvasGeometry.textFrameSize, which estimates when there is no style (0.56 em character width). Aligning plain legacy text will therefore be close but not pixel-exact. Styled text (FEATURE-04) goes through the resolver.
4. The centre clamp (0.05...0.95) means aligning very large items to canvas edges can hit the clamp. translateRigidly limits the delta and reports partial application rather than deforming a group.
5. Concurrent wave-2 edits to ThumbnailDocument.swift (templates, portable files, photo adjustments) will conflict textually in ThumbnailDocumentLayer and reconciled(). Keep this diff to about 10 lines and merge after wave 2 lands. Wave-2 code that regenerates layer IDs must call remappingGroupIDs(), or two imported copies could share a group ID.
6. Group rotation with flipped members relies on the modifier order at PremiumPreviewComponentView.swift:258-262 (rotation, then x-flip). If PreviewComponentView orders them differently, the sign logic must be per-editor. Unit tests cover both.
7. The two preview files are large (about 1.4k and 1.6k lines) and most selection-set changes touch them. Isolate the logic behind CanvasArrangementContext and keep export call sites on the nil path.
8. onKeyPress and focus on iPhone without a hardware keyboard are a no-op. The toolbar buttons and numeric inspector remain the accessible path.
9. Image bounds decode UIImage per layer, so it must be cached by layer id. Arrange commands must not run inside a drag's onChanged, only on end, for performance.

gapEvidence:
Checked in /Users/williamjiamin/ThumbnailMaker-work/baseline. None of the four parts of this feature exist today: several sizes in one design, crop or layout overrides per size, a reflow step, and clipping flags.

1. **A document has exactly one canvas.** `ThumbnailDocument` (Models/ThumbnailDocument.swift:139-154) holds one `canvas` (`ThumbnailDocumentCanvas`, :232-245, which is just `aspectRatioRawValue` + `backgroundColor`). It holds one `imageRecipe` (:149) and one set of transforms per layer: `text.transform` (:253), `profile.transform` (:282), and content transform/size/width/height (:349-465). There is no field for another size, override, or linked copy. `grep -i "alternate|format"` in Models finds only export/file-format code.

2. **Changing size overwrites the design.** Each ratio or preset control writes the single `selectedRatio` in place:
   - `ExportSettingsView.swift:76-77` (`options.applyPreset(preset); selectedRatio = preset.aspectRatio`)
   - `CustomizationControlComponentView.swift:81,98`
   - `PremiumCustomizationControlComponentView.swift:81,98`
   - `AspectRatioDrawerView.swift:26`

   The 9:16 "Shorts" preset (`ThumbnailExportModel.swift:160-166`, 1080x1920) and "Instagram Square" (:178-183, 1080x1080) therefore re-letterbox the one landscape design. The original is not kept, and nothing is adjusted to fit.

3. **Text size depends on canvas height, so a plain ratio swap breaks the layout.** A text layer's font is `canvasSize.height * size` (`ThumbnailDocument.swift:64`; `ThumbnailTextStyle.swift:257` "720 * 0.15"). Images use `min(w,h) * size` (:27), and shapes use width/height as fractions of the canvas (:108-111). A 16:9 → 9:16 swap with the same values makes title text about 2.7x larger relative to the width. There is no reflow code.

4. **Nothing reports content clipped by a size change.** `ThumbnailReadinessAnalyzer.swift:79-131` checks only text density, text size in the mobile preview, contrast, and whether an image is present. It never checks layers against the canvas or safe-zone bounds.

5. **Parts already exist that this feature can reuse:**
   - FEATURE-03 recipe (`ThumbnailImageFrameRecipe.swift:36-168`) and the pure solver `ThumbnailImageGeometry.solve` (`ThumbnailImageGeometry.swift:29-60`), which is independent of scale.
   - Settle/mutate/settle intents, where one call is one undo step (`ImageFrameViewModelIntents.swift:13-47`).
   - Full-document history snapshots (`ThumbnailDocumentHistory.swift:21-50`), so any new document field becomes undoable automatically.
   - Per-variant documents (`ThumbnailVariantSet.swift:14-21`), so sizes stored inside the document belong to each A/B/C variant.
   - A preview view driven by a binding (`PreviewComponentView(simpleMakerConfiguration: Binding, width, height, isTextInteractive, safeZone, selectedOverlay:)`, used at `SimpleMakerView.swift:288-295`; `ThumbnailProjectPreviewRenderer.swift:40-45` renders a document outside the editor).
   - Exporter entry points that take any view (`ThumbnailExporter.swift:40-55,128-143`).
   - The project uses `PBXFileSystemSynchronizedRootGroup` (5 hits), so new files need no pbxproj edits.
plan:
GOAL (most valuable end-to-end slice): each design (per A/B/C variant) can hold up to 3 alternate sizes: Landscape 16:9 (1280x720, preset youtube-thumbnail), Square 1:1 (1080x1080, instagram-square), and Vertical 9:16 (1080x1920, shorts). A size is created from a proposed reflow that keeps the image's focal point by reusing FEATURE-03 recipes. It gets its own independent crop and layout. Each layer carries a flag if it clips. Content stays linked to the original, and unlinking is reversible. Each size can be exported. The original design's rendered document is never changed by any size operation. Every size operation is exactly one undo step.

== 2. Pure engines (new, fully unit-testable, no UIKit state) ==
Models/ThumbnailFormatReflow.swift: `static func propose(master: ThumbnailDocument, sourceImageSize: CGSize?, kind:) -> ThumbnailAlternateFormat`. Canvas sizes come from `AspectRatio.dimensions`.

(a) Focal intent via FEATURE-03:
- Solve the master recipe on the master frame. Let `focus` be the center of the resulting `sourceRect` (for `.fit` this is the recipe focus).
- If master is `.fill`: propose `.fill` with the same zoom, and focus passed through `effectiveFocus` for the target frame.
- If master is `.fit`: keep `.fit` if the letterboxed image covers at least 60% of the target canvas area. Otherwise propose `.fill` at `focus`, zoom 1.
- `.stretch` stays `.stretch`.
- The image bytes are never touched.

(b) Text (legacy `text` and text content layers): keep font pixel size relative to the short side: `s1 = s0 * (min0/H0) * (H1/min1)`… — precisely `s1 = s0 * (H0/min0) * (min1/H1)`. Then shrink further if `ContentLayerCanvasGeometry.textFrameSize` (styled text goes through `ThumbnailTextStyleResolver`) exceeds 90% of the target width. Clamp to `textSizeLimits`.

(c) Image and profile layers: size is already relative to min(w,h), so keep it.

(d) Shapes: keep the pixel aspect scaled by min1/min0, then clamp.

(e) Positions: keep normalized x/y, then pull each center inward so its frame fits inside the target preset's safe zone if one exists (`ThumbnailSafeZone.contentRect`), otherwise the canvas. The pull is limited to the 0.05...0.95 clamp. Rotation and flip are kept.

(f) Output: `layout` for every current layer id, `reflowVersion = 1`, and `presetID = kind.presetID`.

Models/ThumbnailFormatResolver.swift:
- `static func resolvedDocument(master:, formatID:) -> ThumbnailDocument?` starts from a copy of master with `formats = nil`, then:
  - sets `canvas.aspectRatioRawValue` = kind ratio and `imageRecipe` = format recipe;
  - for each layer id, applies the `layout` geometry, or for a layer added to the master after the size was created, an on-the-fly `ThumbnailFormatReflow.geometry(for:)` stamped with `reflowVersion`;
  - sets `isVisible = master.isVisible && !hidden`;
  - replaces `text.value` / text content value with `detachedText[id]` when present;
  - sets `export.presetID` = format preset.
- Content (image data, style, colors, font, background color, and wave-2 brand-kit or photo-adjustment fields) is copied from master unchanged. This is the linking.
- `resolvedSimpleConfiguration` / `resolvedPremiumConfiguration` convenience wrappers.

Models/ThumbnailFormatLinker.swift has one pure function:
`foldBack(master: ThumbnailDocument, formatID:, edited: ThumbnailDocument) -> ThumbnailFormatSet`.
- It writes only into the format: `layout[id] = extract(id, edited)`, `imageRecipe = edited.imageRecipe`, hidden set from the visibility diff, `detachedText` for detached ids only, and `presetID`/format only when the chosen preset's ratio matches the kind.
- It never returns a changed master. That structurally guarantees "original design unchanged".
- Layers present in `edited` but not in master are ignored. The size editor offers no add/delete, and a missing layer maps to hidden.

Models/ThumbnailFormatClipping.swift: `analyze(resolved: ThumbnailDocument, sourceImageSize:, safeZone:) -> [ThumbnailFormatClipFlag]`. Each flag is `{layerID, layerName, kind: .outsideCanvas | .outsideSafeZone | .textAtMinimumSize | .imageSubjectCropped}` and has a user-facing message.
- Frames use the same `ContentLayerCanvasGeometry` functions the preview uses, with rotation handled as an AABB of the rotated rect.
- `imageSubjectCropped` fires when the target `sourceRect` covers less than 50% of the master's visible `sourceRect`, measured through `ThumbnailImageGeometry.solve`.
- No scores. These are informational only, matching the variant anti-requirement spirit.

== 3. View-model hooks (new files; VM bodies change by one line each) ==
New ViewModels/ThumbnailFormatViewModelIntents.swift has extensions on both VMs, mirroring `ImageFrameViewModelIntents.swift`. Every intent does `commitEditorStateNow()`, then a single mutation of `configuration.formatSet`, then `commitEditorStateNow()`, which gives exactly one undo step and autosave. Intents:
- `availableFormatKinds`
- `createAlternateFormat(_ kind) -> String?` (reflow proposal; returns nil if it exists or the design is empty)
- `commitAlternateFormatEdit(id, edited: SimpleMakerConfigurationModel)` (uses `ThumbnailFormatLinker`)
- `reproposeAlternateFormat(id)` (keeps `detachedText` and hidden ids)
- `resetFormatLayer(id, layerID)`
- `setFormatLayerHidden`
- `unlinkFormatText(id, layerID)` (copies the current master text into `detachedText`)
- `relinkFormatText(id, layerID)` (drops it; reversible; the undo step restores)
- `removeAlternateFormat(id)`
- `resolvedFormatConfiguration(id)`
- `formatClipFlags(id)`
- `prepareAlternateFormatExport(id, content:)` reuses `ThumbnailExporter.preparedFileExport` with the format's `ThumbnailExportOptions` (`export.makeOptions()` of the resolved doc). The base file name is `variantExportBaseName + "-" + kind.rawValue`. It sets the existing published `fileExport`/`isFileExporterPresented`.

Premium mirror: same API returning `PremiumMakerConfigurationModel`.

The only edits inside the VM files are none needed for the intents (`commitEditorStateNow`, `simpleMakerConfiguration`, `fileExport`, `isFileExporterPresented`, `variantExportBaseName` are already internal). Optional: none. The existing undo/redo, variant switch, and project adopt paths already round-trip `formatSet` through the configuration.

  - An `ImageFrameControlRow` bound to `$working.imageRecipe` (FEATURE-03 reuse).

Link state shows a "Linked to original" label; while linked the text field is disabled with the caption "Edit in the original to change every size". Unlinking enables `formatDetachedTextField`.

- Hooks, about 10-15 lines each:
  - SimpleMakerView.swift: insert `formatStripSection` after `variantBarSection` (around :657-700), add `@State var editingFormatID: String?`, and add one `.sheet(item:)` next to the existing sheets (:107-157).
  - PremiumMakerView.swift: same.

Out of slice (document as follow-ups):
- "Export all sizes" batch across variants (reuse the `ThumbnailVariantExportPlan` pattern).
- Custom sizes beyond the 3 kinds.

== 5. Composition with wave 2 ==
- Portable project files: automatic (document field).
- Personal templates: call `removingFormats()` when saving a template; `applyTemplate` replaces the document content, so `formatSet` goes stale. Resolver tolerates this: missing layer ids fall back to the on-the-fly reflow, and stale layout ids are ignored.
- Brand kits and photo adjustments: they modify master content, which links into every size automatically. The resolver copies all non-geometry fields, so new wave-2 fields need no changes here as long as they are not geometry.
- Variants: `duplicateVariant` copies the document, which copies its sizes, so each A/B/C variant keeps its own sizes.

risks:
1. **Text size rule.** The text-size scale depends on legacy text being height-relative (`ThumbnailTextStyle.swift:257`, `ThumbnailDocument.swift:64`). If the Premium preview sizes legacy text differently, the reflow numbers drift. Pin this with a rendering test using `ImageRenderer` at 1080x1920.

2. **Stale layout ids after a template or suggestion.** A template, suggestion, or idea applied in the main editor replaces content. The layer ids stored in a size's `layout` then no longer match. The resolver must tolerate this: unknown ids are ignored and new ids are reflowed on the fly. The user may see the size re-proposed. Consider auto-clearing sizes on `applyTemplate` as a follow-up.

3. **Merge conflicts with wave 2.** Wave 2 edits the same mapping lines in `ThumbnailDocument.swift` (`init(configuration:)` and `applySharedState`) and the configuration models. Keep the hunks to one line each and do not bump `ThumbnailDocument.currentVersion`, to avoid version conflicts.

4. **Older builds drop sizes.** An older app ignores the `formats` key and drops it on re-save. The data loss is silent but limited to the sizes, and project `schemaVersion` is deliberately left unchanged so older builds can still open projects.

5. **Performance.**
   - `configuration.document` is computed often, so `formatSet` must be a plain value copy. Nothing may be resolved inside `.document`.
   - Chip thumbnails render live previews. Throttle them or render only visible chips, and reuse the `ThumbnailProjectPreviewRenderer` approach if it is slow.
   - Resolving decodes the image once for the source size; cache it by `imageData` hash inside the strip.

6. **Interactive preview inside a sheet.** The interactive PreviewComponentView inside a sheet uses `selectedOverlay` and layer-lock state from the configuration. Verify that gestures work with a local `@State` binding. The fallback is the non-interactive preview plus nudge controls.

7. **Clip flags are approximations.** They use the same estimated text frame as the editor, so they are approximate for unstyled text. The wording must stay informational, with no scores.

8. **Undo jumps.** Undo while the size editor is closed can remove a size the user is looking at in the strip. That is acceptable. The sheet must close if its `formatID` disappears; `.sheet(item:)` bound to an id that is checked against `formatSet` handles this.

plan:
GOAL: an edit that doesn't change a photo never re-encodes, re-hashes or re-inlines that photo. History and variants share one buffer per photo. Heavy image work moves off the main actor. Budgets are explicit and measured.

The slice has 6 steps. Steps 1-4 are the core, step 5 is the storage win, and step 6 moves export encoding and adds guard tests. VM and view edits are limited to a few one-line hooks.

STEP 1: Measurement and budgets (new files)
- ThumbnailMaker/Services/Performance/ThumbnailPerformanceProbe.swift
  - `enum ThumbnailPerfOp: String { documentSnapshot, historyCommit, projectSave, variantSave, draftSave, imageImport, imageEncode, exportRender, exportEncode, undoRedo, variantSwitch }`.
  - `ThumbnailPerformanceProbe.measure<T>(_ op:, _ body: () throws -> T) rethrows -> T` emits an os_signpost interval (OSLog subsystem "ThumbnailMaker", category "Performance") and records to an injectable `ThumbnailPerformanceRecorder`.
  - An async overload for detached work.
- ThumbnailPerformanceRecorder: a lock-protected in-memory ring buffer of `(op, durationMs, footprintBytesAfter)`. `shared` is a no-op in Release. Tests install a capturing recorder.
- ThumbnailMaker/Services/Performance/ThumbnailMemoryFootprint.swift reads `currentBytes()` via `task_info(TASK_VM_INFO).phys_footprint`, plus `peakSince(mark:)` using the recorder samples.
- ThumbnailMaker/Models/ThumbnailPerformanceBudget.swift holds static budgets, documented as targets for a 12 MP (4032x3024) photo on an A15 device:
  - text-edit commit (snapshot + history + save) at most 16 ms on main when the image is unchanged
  - undo/redo at most 50 ms
  - variant switch at most 100 ms
  - project save of an unchanged image: 0 PNG encodes and 0 SHA hashes
  - import to editable at most 1.5 s, with the PNG encode off main
  - export 4K PNG: render on main at most 400 ms, encode off main
  - peak footprint while editing at most 450 MB
  - total history payload across all variant slots at most 256 MB (`historyPayloadByteBudget`)
  - import decode cap: long edge 4096 px by default (`maxImportLongEdge`); this keeps 12 MP intact and caps 48 MP ProRAW-class inputs
- Probes wrap existing calls through tiny hooks, one `ThumbnailPerformanceProbe.measure(.x) { ... }` wrapper each: commitEditorStateNow, saveDraftNow, undo/redo in both VMs, and the export funnel.

STEP 2: Payload cache, so there are no re-encodes on text edits (new file plus a small edit in ThumbnailDocument.swift)
- New ThumbnailMaker/Models/ThumbnailEncodedImageCache.swift.
  - `final class ThumbnailEncodedImageCache: @unchecked Sendable`, lock protected, backed by `NSMapTable<UIImage, Entry>.weakToStrongObjects()`.
  - Entry holds `data: Data` (the PNG) and a lazily computed `digest: String`.
  - API:
    - `encodedPNG(for image:) -> Data?`: on a miss, encode (with the existing orientation-normalization logic moved here) and store; on a hit, return the same Data value, so its buffer is shared.
    - `register(_ image: UIImage, encoded data: Data)`
    - `image(decoding data: Data) -> UIImage?`: decodes and registers the pair, so a document-to-configuration-to-document round trip does not re-encode.
    - `digest(for data: Data) -> String`: looks up an entry whose buffer is identical (same `withUnsafeBytes` baseAddress and count, which means byte-identical immutable storage); otherwise it hashes and memoizes in a small digest LRU keyed by buffer identity.
    - `prewarm(_ image:) async`: runs the encode inside `Task.detached(priority: .userInitiated)`.
    - `removeAll()` for tests and memory warnings.
  - It observes `UIApplication.didReceiveMemoryWarningNotification` and drops entries for images that are no longer alive (the weak keys already do this).
- ThumbnailDocument.swift edits:
  - `encodedImageData(from:)` (1421-1437) becomes a one-line delegate to `ThumbnailEncodedImageCache.shared.encodedPNG(for:)`.
  - The `UIImage.init(data:)` calls at 1372, 1382 and 1402 become `ThumbnailEncodedImageCache.shared.image(decoding:)`.
  - This keeps the document format byte-identical (still PNG with the same normalization), so it is fully back-compatible. Existing ThumbnailImagePersistenceTests keep passing.

risks:
- **Buffer-identity equality:** the history fast path and digest reuse depend on Foundation Data sharing its buffer through copy-on-write, and they compare baseAddress plus count. Identical immutable storage is byte-identical, so this is safe, but a Data slice with an offset could miss the fast path. That only costs speed, never correctness. A unit test pins it.
- **Weak-key cache on UIImage:** if code creates new UIImage instances from the same pixels (for example crop or background-removal results), they are real re-encodes. That is correct but still costs time. Make sure the crop and cutout paths register their output.
- **Import downsampling changes stored pixels for inputs above 4096 px:** frame recipes are normalized, so framing survives. Export quality at 4K presets is unaffected, but any expectation of full-resolution 48 MP storage changes. Keep the cap configurable.
- **Sidecar assets are a new on-disk shape:** an old build reading a new variants file loses images, which surface as missingAssetDigests. Crash-safety risks are orphaned sidecars (mitigated by GC after a successful JSON write) and a JSON written before its sidecars (write sidecars first).
- **Composition with wave 2:** portable project files must package the sidecars. Photo adjustments must stay recipe-based or register their baked output. Brand kits and personal templates flow through ThumbnailDocument, which now gets the cache automatically. Merge conflicts are likely in ThumbnailDocument.swift near encodedImageData and in the VM export call sites.
- **Skipping unchanged saves:** it leaves metadata.updatedAt unchanged. A library sort that relies on a touch-on-open would change, so verify ThumbnailProjectLibraryTests.
- **Off-main export encoding:** UIImage must not be mutated during encode; exporter images are freshly rendered and immutable, so this is fine. Actor-isolation warnings under Swift 6 strict concurrency may need `@unchecked Sendable` wrappers.
- **Memory-warning eviction:** it must not evict entries still referenced by a live configuration. The weak keys ensure that.
- **Timing budgets are flaky on simulators and CI:** gate on event counts (encodes and hashes) rather than milliseconds.
